Wage Distributions and the Bite of Minimum Wages Across Philippine Regions

National Analysis Using Harmonized LFS Microdata, 2004–2025 — v5 (Companion to the NCR Proof of Concept)

AJ Montesa

July 24, 2026

1 Overview

This document extends the NCR proof of concept (ncr_mw_proof_of_concept_v5.Rmd) to a national, all-region analysis of Philippine wage distributions and the bite of regional minimum wages, using the v8 harmonized LFS microdata (2004 Q1 – 2025 Q2, 86 quarterly rounds). It is the third document in the minimum-wage series:

  1. Minimum Wages and Inflation — real erosion of regional wage orders.
  2. Minimum Wages and Productivity — wage floors vs. labour productivity.
  3. This document — where the wage floor sits inside the observed wage distribution, region by region.

Following Cengiz, Dube, Lindner & Zipperer (2019), we keep four concepts separate: statutory bindingness (Kaitz index, share at/below the floor), observed bunching (mass near the floor), noncompliance (mass strictly below the floor, with the coverage caveats that phrase requires), and causal employment effects. This document delivers the first three descriptively at national scale, adds a descriptive stacked event-study approximation of the Cengiz bunching design around wage-order increases (N14), and produces — as saved artifacts — the region × quarter × wage-bin panels (nominal MW-relative, N8, and spatially-indexed real-peso, N13) that any future causal stacked-DiD analysis would consume. It deliberately does not attempt causal estimation: the event study is a before/after description with an internal pre-trend check, no more.

1.1 Headline conventions (changes relative to the NCR PoC)

These were agreed in the design discussion; each is implemented and cross-checked below, and the Reconciliation section reconciles NCR numbers under old vs. new conventions.

Convention NCR PoC This document (headline)
Analysis sample for Kaitz / bunching / bins Private Establishment + Government/GOCC + Private Household, all industries Sample C: Private Establishment, non-agriculture only (Government and Private Household reported as separate reference modules)
“At MW” band ±₱25 in real 2018 PHP ±5% of the applicable MW (scale-invariant across regions); real ±₱25 retained as sensitivity
MW threshold NCR Non-Ag single rate Regional non-agriculture rates as a min–max interval (total_min, total_max); basic_* as sensitivity
Deflator national CPI Regional CPI, pre-NIR configuration (CPI_noNIR.xlsx), 2018 = 100
Geography NCR only 17 wage-board lineages (see the lineage recode section); every headline chart shown as national aggregate and regional facets
Poverty thresholds — (a single region needs no spatial index) Primary: spatial price index \(\theta_r\) = 2018 threshold ratio to NCR, making real-₱25 bands mean the same purchasing power in every region (CPI indexes time; \(\theta\) indexes place). Auxiliary: wage-adequacy benchmark (family of 5, 1 earner, 313 factor days)

1.2 Reading guide for units and bands

Different statistics live on different scales, deliberately:

  • Scale-free statistics (Kaitz index, share below MW, ±5% at-band, log-distance bunching histograms): computed on nominal wages against the nominal contemporaneous MW. Because both sides are deflated by the same regional CPI, deflation cancels; nominal and real give identical numbers for these ratios.
  • Cross-year absolute comparisons (wage levels, distribution snapshots, poverty-wage overlays): real 2018 PHP, deflated by the regional CPI.
  • Wage-bin objects (the ₱25-bin panels in the wage-bin section): two complementary scales. The nominal panel bins \((w - MW)\) in contemporaneous pesos (the raw Cengiz unit). The spatially-indexed real panel (N13) bins \((w^{real} - MW^{real})/\theta_r\) in NCR-2018-equivalent pesos — CPI indexes time, the 2018 poverty-threshold ratios index place — which is the unit in which bins can be summed nationally and events averaged across regions.

2 Notation and Formulas

Every statistic below is defined here before any code computes it. Each computing chunk restates, in comments, the formula it implements, so the code can be audited line-by-line against this section.

Indexing. \(i\) indexes person-quarter observations; \(r\) indexes wage-board lineages (lineage recode section); \(t\) indexes LFS rounds, anchored at reference date \(d_t\) = the first day of the survey reference month (Jan 1 / Apr 1 / Jul 1 / Oct 1); \(m(d)\) = the calendar month containing date \(d\). \(w_i\) is reported daily basic pay (basic_pay_php, already daily-equivalent in the PUF); \(\omega_i\) is the LFS sampling weight (weight).

(N1) Weighted empirical CDF and quantiles. For a set \(S\) of observations, \[\hat F_S(x) \;=\; \frac{\sum_{i \in S} \omega_i\,\mathbf 1[w_i \le x]}{\sum_{i \in S} \omega_i}, \qquad Q_S(p) \;=\; \min\{\,x \in \{w_i\}_{i\in S} : \hat F_S(x) \ge p\,\}.\] \(Q_S(p)\) is the left-continuous inverse (a step function taking observed values only). This matches the weighted_quantile() helper exactly — no interpolation between order statistics.

(N2) As-of minimum-wage assignment. Let \(E_r = \{e_1 < e_2 < \dots\}\) be the effectivity dates of lineage \(r\)’s wage-order rows (each tranche is its own row). For any date \(d\): \[MW_r(d) \;=\; \text{rate of the row with effectivity } \max\{e \in E_r : e \le d\}.\] Applied to each of the four rate columns, giving \(MW^{tot,max}_r(d),\; MW^{tot,min}_r(d),\; MW^{bas,max}_r(d),\; MW^{bas,min}_r(d)\). The headline threshold is \(MW^{tot,max}\) (highest non-agriculture total rate — the doc-1 convention); \(MW^{tot,min}\) bounds the analysis from below (N5). Because \(d_t\) is the first day of the reference month, a wage order effective mid-month is assigned only from the following round — the same anchoring convention as the NCR PoC (its WO-25 note).

(N3) Regional CPI deflator. Let \(CPI_{r,m}\) be the all-items index for lineage \(r\) in month \(m\) from the pre-NIR workbook (chained across base periods by PSA; continuity verified at each sheet junction below). Define the region base \(\overline{CPI}_r^{2018} = \tfrac{1}{12}\sum_{m \in 2018} CPI_{r,m}\) and \[w^{real}_i \;=\; w_i \times \frac{\overline{CPI}_r^{2018}}{CPI_{r,\,m(d_t)}}.\] If the workbook is exactly 2018-based, \(\overline{CPI}_r^{2018} = 100\) and this reduces to \(w_i \times 100 / CPI_{r,m}\); the rebasing step makes that an identity we verify rather than assume.

(N4) Bindingness statistics (computed on Sample C, per \(r,t\) cell, against \(MW = MW^{tot,max}_r(d_t)\) unless stated):

  • Kaitz (median): \(\;K^{med}_{r,t} = MW / Q_{r,t}(0.5)\); Kaitz (mean): \(K^{mean}_{r,t} = MW / \bar w_{r,t}\) with \(\bar w_{r,t} = \sum \omega_i w_i / \sum \omega_i\).
  • Share at-or-below: \(\;F_{r,t}(MW) = \hat F_{r,t}(MW)\) (weak inequality).
  • Strict noncompliance share: \(\;B_{r,t} = \sum \omega_i \mathbf 1[w_i < MW] / \sum \omega_i\).

(N5) The min–max noncompliance interval. With multiple rates inside a region, one collapsed threshold cannot classify every worker correctly. We bound: \[B^{min}_{r,t} = \Pr_\omega\!\big[w_i < MW^{tot,min}\big] \;\le\; \text{true noncompliance} \;\le\; B^{max}_{r,t} = \Pr_\omega\!\big[w_i < MW^{tot,max}\big].\] \(B^{min}\) counts only workers below every applicable rate (definite subminimum pay); \(B^{max}\) adds workers between the lowest and highest rate, whose status depends on unobserved sub-regional/establishment coverage. Charts draw the ribbon between the two.

(N6) Compliance partition (±5% band). With \(\rho_i = w_i / MW - 1\): \[\text{below: } \rho_i < -0.05; \qquad \text{at: } |\rho_i| \le 0.05; \qquad \text{above: } \rho_i > 0.05.\] The three weighted shares partition Sample C exactly (each observation in exactly one class). Note “below” here is \(w_i < 0.95\,MW\) — a band boundary — and is therefore not the same object as the strict noncompliance share \(B_{r,t}\) in (N4); both are reported. Sensitivity band: \(|w^{real}_i - MW^{real}| \le 25\,\theta_r\) in 2018 PHP — the PoC’s real-₱25 band, spatially indexed per (N13) so its purchasing-power width is the same in every region (in NCR, \(\theta = 1\), it is exactly the PoC band).

(N7) Log-distance bunching histogram. For bin width \(h = 0.025\) log points and bin index \(k\), the weighted share in bin \(k\) is \[s_k = \frac{\sum_i \omega_i\,\mathbf 1\big[\,k h \le \log w_i - \log MW_{r(i)}(d_{t(i)}) < (k+1)h\,\big]}{\sum_i \omega_i},\] pooled over all region-quarters (each worker measured against their own contemporaneous regional floor).

(N8) ₱25 wage-bin panel. Bin edges \(b \in \{-300, -275, \dots, 600\}\) (left-closed): observation \(i\) falls in bin \(b\) if \(b \le w_i - MW^{tot,max}_{r}(d_t) < b + 25\) (nominal pesos). The panel records, per \((r, t, b)\): unweighted count, summed weight, and weighted share of the \((r,t)\) cell. Saved to Output/ in the wage-bin section.

(N9) Poverty-threshold daily-wage equivalent. From the PSA annual per-capita threshold \(PT^{pc}_{r,y}\) (survey years \(y\)): \[PT^{wage}_{r,y} \;=\; PT^{pc}_{r,y} \times \frac{\text{FAMILY\_SIZE}}{\text{EARNERS} \times \text{FACTOR\_DAYS}} \;=\; PT^{pc}_{r,y} \times \frac{5}{1 \times 313},\] the daily basic wage at which one earner, paid every DOLE factor day (365 − 52 rest days = 313), keeps a family of five exactly at the poverty line. All three constants are setup parameters; the ÷365 calendar-day variant is shown as an alternative in the poverty-benchmark section.

(N10) Monthly projection of the threshold (headline: CPI projection). With \(y^*(m) = \max\{y \in Y_r : y \le \text{year}(m)\}\) (latest survey year not after \(m\)) and \(\overline{CPI}_{r,y}\) = the mean of monthly CPI over calendar year \(y\): \[PT^{wage}_{r,m} \;=\; PT^{wage}_{r,y^*} \times \frac{CPI_{r,m}}{\overline{CPI}_{r,y^*}}.\] This holds the threshold constant in real terms between survey years — the same logic PSA uses for inter-FIES updates — and extrapolates 2024–2025 from the 2023 base. Sensitivity: linear interpolation in nominal levels between survey-year anchors placed at July 1 of each survey year, with no extrapolation beyond the last anchor. The poverty-threshold preparation section overlays the two.

(N11) Aggregation to the national level. Shares and histogram statistics aggregate by person-level pooling against each worker’s own regional floor — e.g. the national strict-noncompliance share is \[B^{nat}_t = \frac{\sum_{i \in t} \omega_i\,\mathbf 1[w_i < MW_{r(i)}(d_t)]}{\sum_{i \in t} \omega_i},\] not a comparison to any national rate (none exists). The Kaitz index has no national statutory referent, so the “national” Kaitz is reported as the covered-employment-weighted mean of regional indices, \(K^{nat}_t = \sum_r \Omega_{r,t} K_{r,t} / \sum_r \Omega_{r,t}\) with \(\Omega_{r,t} = \sum_{i \in r,t} \omega_i\), drawn with the cross-region min–max range shaded.

(N12) Heaping shares. For divisor \(d \in \{5, 10, 50, 100\}\): \(H_d = \Pr_\omega[\,w_i \bmod d = 0\,]\) (weighted share of wage reports exactly divisible by \(d\)).

(N13) Spatial price index and comparable real-peso bands. The regional CPI (N3) indexes prices over time within a region but says nothing about price-level differences across regions: a real 2018 ₱25 in NCR is not the same purchasing power as a real 2018 ₱25 in BARMM, so the NCR PoC’s ±₱25 band does not transfer to a national analysis unmodified. The regional poverty thresholds are priced at local costs, so their cross-region ratios provide the missing spatial deflator. Define, from the 2018 (No-NIR vintage) per-capita thresholds, \[\theta_r \;=\; \frac{PT^{pc}_{r,2018}}{PT^{pc}_{NCR,2018}}, \qquad \theta_{NCR} = 1,\] (the family-size / earner / factor-day constants of N9 cancel in the ratio, so \(\theta_r\) does not depend on the poverty-wage construct). The spatially-and-temporally adjusted wage and floor are \[\tilde w_i = \frac{w^{real}_i}{\theta_{r(i)}}, \qquad \tilde M_{r,t} = \frac{MW^{tot,max}_{r}(d_t)/\text{defl}_{r,m}}{\theta_r},\] both in NCR-2018-equivalent pesos. A ±₱25 band on this scale is the same real band everywhere: in region \(r\)’s own 2018 pesos it has width \(25\,\theta_r\), scaled to local price levels. Real wage bins are then left-closed ₱25 bins of \(\tilde w_i - \tilde M_{r,t}\) — distance from the real minimum wage — over \(\{-300, \dots, 600\}\); because every term is in one common unit, bin masses are summable across regions and years, and in NCR (\(\theta = 1\)) the construction reduces exactly to the PoC’s.

(N14) Wage-increase event study (Cengiz-style, stacked, with timing-based controls). An event \(e = (r, t_0)\) is the first LFS round at which the as-of assignment (N2) delivers a new, higher \(MW^{tot,max}\) with nominal size \(\Delta_e = MW^{new}/MW^{old} - 1 \ge 3\%\). Event time \(\tau = t - t_0\) spans \([-4, +7]\) (pre-window \([-4,-1]\), matching the PoC), post-side censored at the lineage’s next event. The event’s floor is fixed in NCR-2018-equivalent pesos (N13): \(\tilde M_e = MW^{new}_r(t_0) / (\text{defl}_{r,m(t_0)}\,\theta_r)\). For real ₱25 bins \(b\) of \(\tilde w_i - \tilde M_e\) over \([-300, 600)\), the outcome is bin employment per working-age person (per-capita counts, not shares — shares can only show redistribution, never employment loss): \[E_{e,\tau,b} = \frac{\sum_{i \in C_{r,t_0+\tau},\,b} \omega_i}{\text{WAP}_{r,\,t_0+\tau}}, \qquad \Delta E_{e,\tau,b} = E_{e,\tau,b} - \tfrac{1}{4}\textstyle\sum_{\tau'=-4}^{-1} E_{e,\tau',b}.\] Controls. For each event, control lineages are those with no own event within \([t_0-4,\,t_0+4]\); their bins are measured against the treated event’s \(\tilde M_e\) — meaningful only because N13 puts all regions on one real-peso scale. The DiD contrast is \(\Delta E^{DiD}_{e,\tau,b} = \Delta E^{treat}_{e,\tau,b} - \overline{\Delta E}^{ctrl}_{e,\tau,b}\) (equal-weighted control mean), reported for events with ≥ 3 controls. Summary statistics (post = mean over \(\tau \in [0,3]\), equal-weighted across events), following the PoC’s grid: missing mass \(\Delta b = \sum_{b<0} \Delta E\); excess mass \(\Delta a(B^*) = \sum_{0 \le b < B^*} \Delta E\) for \(B^* \in \{100, 200, 300\}\); net low-wage change \(\Delta b + \Delta a(B^*)\); bunching ratio \(\Delta a / |\Delta b|\); and the upper-tail placebo \(\sum_{300 \le b < 600} \Delta E\), which should be ≈ 0 if changes are localised at the floor. Uncertainty: percentile confidence intervals from a nonparametric bootstrap over events (resampling whole events, 500 draws). Identification caveat: the control set is selected on wage-order timing, not random assignment; no never-treated region exists, and control availability is concentrated in freeze episodes (2009–10, 2020–21). This is the closest feasible approximation to Cengiz et al., not a replication of their identification.

3 Setup

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
library(readxl)
library(knitr)

# kableExtra is used for table styling when available; the document knits
# without it (plain kable) so the pipeline has no hard dependency on it.
HAS_KE <- requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)
if (HAS_KE) library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# ---- Helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

# (N1) Weighted quantile: left-continuous inverse of the weighted ECDF.
# Q(p) = min{ x in observed values : Fhat(x) >= p }. No interpolation.
weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) return(rep(NA_real_, length(probs)))
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w) & w > 0
  x <- x[keep]; w <- w[keep]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, length(probs)))
  ord <- order(x); x <- x[ord]; w <- w[ord]
  cumw <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  vapply(probs, function(p) x[which(cumw >= p)[1]], numeric(1))
}

# Weighted mean (explicit, NA-safe)
wmean <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w)
  if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(x[keep] * w[keep]) / sum(w[keep])
}

# Weighted share of a logical condition
wshare <- function(cond, w) wmean(as.numeric(cond), w)

# Styled table wrapper (falls back to plain kable without kableExtra)
kt <- function(df, cap, digits = getOption("digits"), ...) {
  k <- kable(df, caption = cap, digits = digits, ...)
  if (HAS_KE) {
    k %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                        full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13)
  } else k
}

wrap_text <- function(x, width = 95) paste(strwrap(x, width = width), collapse = "\n")

# ---- Project constants -----------------------------------------------------

# Fixed wage-board lineage order used in EVERY faceted chart and table.
REGION_ORDER <- c("NCR", "CAR", "I", "II", "III", "IV-A", "IV-B", "V",
                  "VI", "VII", "VIII", "IX", "X", "XI", "XII", "XIII",
                  "ARMM-BARMM")

# (N6) headline at-MW band: +/- 5% of the applicable MW
AT_MW_BAND_PCT   <- 0.05
# sensitivity band: +/- 25 real 2018 PHP (NCR PoC convention)
AT_MW_BAND_PHP_REAL <- 25
BASE_YEAR        <- 2018L

# (N8) wage-bin construction (nominal PHP relative to MW^{tot,max})
BIN_PHP    <- 25
BIN_LO     <- -300
BIN_HI     <- 600

# (N7) log-distance histogram bin width (log points)
LOG_BIN_H  <- 0.025
LOG_BIN_LIM <- 0.70

# (N13) spatially comparable real bins: P25 width in NCR-2018-equivalent
# pesos, relative to the REAL minimum wage; theta_r built at run time from
# the 2018 poverty thresholds
SPATIAL_BASE <- "NCR"       # numeraire lineage for theta (theta_NCR = 1)
BIN_REAL_LO <- -300
BIN_REAL_HI <- 600

# (N14) wage-increase event study (Cengiz-style)
EVENT_MIN_NOM_PCT <- 0.03   # prominence screen: nominal increase >= 3%
EVENT_PRE_Q       <- 4      # pre-window: tau in [-4, -1] (PoC convention)
EVENT_POST_Q      <- 7      # max post-window: tau in [0, +7], censored at
                            # the next event in the same lineage
EVENT_BIN_LO      <- -300   # event bins: NCR-2018-equivalent pesos
EVENT_BIN_HI      <-  600   # relative to the NEW real floor, P25 width
EXCESS_GRID       <- c(100, 200, 300)  # B* grid for excess mass (PoC)
PLACEBO_LO        <- 300    # upper-tail placebo zone: [300, 600)
MIN_CONTROLS      <- 3      # events need >= this many clean controls (DiD)
N_BOOT            <- 500    # bootstrap draws over events
set.seed(20260724)

# (N9) poverty-wage conversion parameters
FAMILY_SIZE <- 5
EARNERS     <- 1
FACTOR_DAYS <- 313      # 365 - 52 rest days (DOLE factor-day convention)
FACTOR_DAYS_ALT <- 365  # calendar-day variant shown in the poverty-benchmark section

# Percentile grid
PCTL_GRID <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95)

# Sample-C definition (see Sample Construction)
COVERED_CLASS <- "Private Establishment"
WAGE_CLASS_LABELS <- c("Private Establishment", "Government/GOCC",
                       "Private Household")

MIN_CELL_N <- params$min_cell_n

4 Data Preparation

4.1 Load harmonized LFS and assert the required schema

Rather than auto-detecting columns, this document asserts the exact columns it needs and stops with a diagnostic if any is missing — a schema mismatch should fail at the top, not corrupt charts downstream.

lfs_raw <- read_rds(params$lfs_path)

required_cols <- c("year", "quarter", "month", "region", "province",
                   "weight", "male", "age_years", "educ_5cat",
                   "class_label", "ind_section", "payment_label",
                   "basic_pay_php", "employed")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(lfs_raw))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("LFS file is missing required columns: ",
       paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       "\nColumns present: ", paste(sort(names(lfs_raw)), collapse = ", "))
}

cat("Rows:", comma(nrow(lfs_raw)), "  Cols:", ncol(lfs_raw), "\n")
## Rows: 18,825,641   Cols: 75
cat("Years:", paste(range(lfs_raw$year, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-"), "\n")
## Years: 2004-2025

4.2 Wage-board lineage recode (region_wb)

The raw LFS region codes migrate over the sample, as established from the weighted-population tabulation (LFS_-_Region.xlsx):

  • 41/42 = IV-A / IV-B through 2016 Q1; 4/17 from 2016 Q2 onward.
  • 15 = ARMM through 2023 Q3; 19 = BARMM from 2023 Q4. One wage-board lineage (ARMM-BARMM).
  • 18 = NIR, present only in 2016 Q4 and 2025 Q1–Q2. There is no NIR wage board in the wage-order panel, so NIR observations are mapped back to the VI / VII lineages via province (45 = Negros Occidental → VI; 46 = Negros Oriental, 61 = Siquijor → VII), mirroring the harmonization script’s region_standard construction. NIR rows with missing province cannot be assigned and are excluded with an explicit count below.
  • All other codes map one-to-one (13 = NCR, 14 = CAR, 16 = XIII/Caraga, 1–12 = Regions I–XII).

Note this recode is built from the raw region variable, not region_standard: the v8 documentation states region_standard spans 1–17, but the raw codes demonstrably include 41/42 pre-2016 Q2, and region_standard passes non-Negros codes through unchanged — so it would carry 41/42 in early years. Building the lineage here, from raw codes, with a full validation crosstab, removes that ambiguity.

# The raw codes in the harmonized file are ZERO-PADDED STRINGS ("01".."19",
# "41", "42"). All matching is therefore done on the INTEGER value of the
# code, which is invariant to padding ("01", "1", and numeric 1 all map
# identically). The mapping is UNCONDITIONAL on date because no integer code
# is reused with a different meaning: 4/17 do not occur before 2016 Q2,
# 41/42 do not occur after 2016 Q1, 19 does not occur before 2023 Q4. The
# crosstab below verifies this empirically on the loaded file.
lfs <- lfs_raw %>%
  mutate(
    region_chr   = str_trim(as.character(region)),
    region_int   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(region_chr)),
    province_int = suppressWarnings(as.integer(str_trim(as.character(province)))),
    region_wb = case_when(
      region_int == 13L ~ "NCR",
      region_int == 14L ~ "CAR",
      region_int == 1L  ~ "I",
      region_int == 2L  ~ "II",
      region_int == 3L  ~ "III",
      region_int %in% c(41L, 4L)  ~ "IV-A",
      region_int %in% c(42L, 17L) ~ "IV-B",
      region_int == 5L  ~ "V",
      region_int == 6L  ~ "VI",
      region_int == 7L  ~ "VII",
      region_int == 8L  ~ "VIII",
      region_int == 9L  ~ "IX",
      region_int == 10L ~ "X",
      region_int == 11L ~ "XI",
      region_int == 12L ~ "XII",
      region_int == 16L ~ "XIII",
      region_int %in% c(15L, 19L) ~ "ARMM-BARMM",
      # NIR: assign by province; NA province -> NA (excluded, counted below)
      region_int == 18L & province_int == 45L              ~ "VI",
      region_int == 18L & province_int %in% c(46L, 61L)    ~ "VII",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    region_wb = factor(region_wb, levels = REGION_ORDER),
    # LFS reference date: first day of the survey reference month (N2 anchor)
    ref_date  = make_date(year, month, 1L)
  )

4.2.1 Validation: raw-code × period crosstab and unmapped rows

# Every raw code should appear only in its expected era, and every row
# should map to a lineage except NIR-with-missing-province.
code_era <- lfs %>%
  mutate(era = case_when(
    year < 2016 | (year == 2016 & quarter == 1) ~ "2004Q1-2016Q1",
    year < 2023 | (year == 2023 & quarter <= 3) ~ "2016Q2-2023Q3",
    TRUE                                        ~ "2023Q4-2025Q2"
  )) %>%
  count(era, region_int) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L) %>%
  arrange(region_int)

kt(code_era, "Raw region codes (integer value) by era, row counts. Expect 41/42 only in the first era, 4/17 only after, 15 only through 2023 Q3, 19 only after, 18 only in NIR quarters.")

4.3 Wage orders: load, lineage mapping, and as-of assignment

The regional wage-order panel (wage_orders_regional.csv) carries, per region × effectivity date, non-agriculture rates only (confirmed by the compiler): basic_min/max, allowance_min/max, total_min/max. Each tranche is its own row keyed by effectivity_date, so the as-of join (N2) needs no special tranche handling. Six rows carry CHECK: effectivity precedes date issued in source; per the doc-1 convention these are used as-is and surfaced below, not adjudicated.

Lineage mapping on the wage-order side:

  • ARMM and BARMM rows are concatenated into the single ARMM-BARMM lineage (BARMM legally succeeded ARMM’s wage board).
  • Pre-split IV rows (all pre-2002) are duplicated into both IV-A and IV-B lineages, so that an as-of lookup early in a lineage’s life still finds the inherited Region IV rate. This affects no 2004+ assignment in practice (both boards issued post-split orders before 2004) but makes the join total rather than partial.
mw_raw <- read_csv(params$mw_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# CHECK-flagged rows: surfaced, used as-is (doc-1 convention). The display
# is capped; the count line is the audit trail.
mw_check <- mw_raw %>%
  filter(str_detect(coalesce(notes, ""), "CHECK")) %>%
  select(region, wage_order, effectivity_date, total_min, total_max, notes)
cat("CHECK-flagged wage-order rows (used as-is):", nrow(mw_check),
    "of", nrow(mw_raw), "\n")

           min(10, nrow(mw_check)), nrow(mw_check)))

mw_lineage <- mw_raw %>%
  mutate(effectivity_date = as.Date(effectivity_date)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(effectivity_date)) %>%
  # region -> lineage
  mutate(region_wb = case_when(
    region %in% c("ARMM", "BARMM") ~ "ARMM-BARMM",
    TRUE ~ region
  )) %>%
  # duplicate pre-split Region IV rows into both successor lineages
  (\(d) bind_rows(
     d %>% filter(region_wb != "IV"),
     d %>% filter(region_wb == "IV") %>% mutate(region_wb = "IV-A"),
     d %>% filter(region_wb == "IV") %>% mutate(region_wb = "IV-B")
  ))() %>%
  mutate(region_wb = factor(region_wb, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(region_wb)) %>%
  select(region_wb, wage_order, effectivity_date,
         basic_min, basic_max, total_min, total_max, notes) %>%
  arrange(region_wb, effectivity_date) %>%
  # if two rows share an effectivity date within a lineage (e.g. an
  # ARMM/BARMM handover artifact), keep the LAST row after sorting --
  # i.e., the later-listed (successor) rate.
  group_by(region_wb, effectivity_date) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()

cat("Wage-order rows after lineage mapping:", nrow(mw_lineage), "\n")
## Wage-order rows after lineage mapping: 566
cat("Lineages covered:", n_distinct(mw_lineage$region_wb), "of",
    length(REGION_ORDER), "\n")
## Lineages covered: 17 of 17
# (N2) as-of assignment: MW_r(d) = rate at max{ e in E_r : e <= d }
assign_mw_lineage <- function(dates, lineage, rate_col) {
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(dates))
  for (rg in levels(mw_lineage$region_wb)) {
    sub <- mw_lineage %>% filter(region_wb == rg)
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) next
    idx_rows <- which(lineage == rg)
    if (length(idx_rows) == 0) next
    pos <- findInterval(dates[idx_rows], sub$effectivity_date)  # 0 if before first e
    ok  <- pos >= 1
    out[idx_rows[ok]] <- sub[[rate_col]][pos[ok]]
  }
  out
}

4.4 Regional CPI: parse, chain-continuity check, and deflators

The primary CPI source is CPI_noNIR.xlsx (pre-NIR configuration: Regions VI/VII include Negros, matching the lineage geography). The current-configuration workbook (CPI.xlsx, with NIR broken out and VI/VII recomputed) is loaded only for a configuration-difference table. Sheets are monthly, wide by "YYYY Mon" columns with "YYYY Ave" columns dropped; the three sheets needed for 1994–2025 appear pre-chained to 2018 = 100 by PSA — the continuity check below verifies this at each sheet junction instead of assuming it.

# Region label -> lineage mapping for the CPI workbooks
cpi_region_map <- c(
  "National Capital Region (NCR)"            = "NCR",
  "Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR)"   = "CAR",
  "Region I (Ilocos Region)"                 = "I",
  "Region II (Cagayan Valley)"               = "II",
  "Region III (Central Luzon)"               = "III",
  "Region IV-A (CALABARZON)"                 = "IV-A",
  "MIMAROPA Region"                          = "IV-B",
  "Region V (Bicol Region)"                  = "V",
  "Region VI (Western Visayas)"              = "VI",
  "Region VII (Central Visayas)"             = "VII",
  "Region VIII (Eastern Visayas)"            = "VIII",
  "Region IX (Zamboanga Peninsula)"          = "IX",
  "Region X (Northern Mindanao)"             = "X",
  "Region XI (Davao Region)"                 = "XI",
  "Region XII (SOCCSKSARGEN)"                = "XII",
  "Region XIII (Caraga)"                     = "XIII",
  "Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM)" = "ARMM-BARMM"
)

# Parse one sheet: wide "YYYY Mon" columns -> long (region_wb, cpi_month, cpi)
parse_cpi_sheet <- function(path, sheet) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = sheet)
  names(raw)[1:2] <- c("geo", "commodity")
  raw %>%
    mutate(geo_clean = str_remove(str_trim(geo), "^\\.+")) %>%
    filter(str_starts(geo, "\\.\\.") & !str_starts(geo, "\\.\\.\\.\\."),
           geo_clean %in% names(cpi_region_map)) %>%
    mutate(region_wb = cpi_region_map[geo_clean]) %>%
    select(region_wb, matches("^\\d{4} ")) %>%
    # recent-month columns can arrive as character (blank / ".." cells);
    # coerce everything to character first, numeric after the pivot
    mutate(across(-region_wb, as.character)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-region_wb, names_to = "ym", values_to = "cpi") %>%
    filter(!str_ends(ym, "Ave")) %>%
    mutate(yr  = as.integer(str_sub(ym, 1, 4)),
           mon = match(str_sub(ym, 6), month.abb),
           cpi_month = make_date(yr, mon, 1),
           cpi = as.numeric(cpi)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cpi)) %>%
    select(region_wb, cpi_month, cpi)
}

cpi_sheets <- c("1994-2006", "2006-2017", "2018-")
cpi_long <- map(cpi_sheets, ~ parse_cpi_sheet(params$cpi_path, .x)) %>%
  list_rbind() %>%
  distinct(region_wb, cpi_month, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # guard vs overlap
  mutate(region_wb = factor(region_wb, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  arrange(region_wb, cpi_month)

cat("CPI region-months parsed:", comma(nrow(cpi_long)),
    " | coverage:", format(min(cpi_long$cpi_month)), "to",
    format(max(cpi_long$cpi_month)), "\n")
## CPI region-months parsed: 6,392  | coverage: 1994-01-01 to 2025-04-01
# National (PHILIPPINES) series, used only in the NCR reconciliation section
parse_cpi_national <- function(path, sheet) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = sheet)
  names(raw)[1:2] <- c("geo", "commodity")
  raw %>% filter(str_trim(geo) == "PHILIPPINES") %>%
    select(matches("^\\d{4} ")) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "ym", values_to = "cpi") %>%
    filter(!str_ends(ym, "Ave")) %>%
    mutate(yr = as.integer(str_sub(ym, 1, 4)),
           mon = match(str_sub(ym, 6), month.abb),
           cpi_month = make_date(yr, mon, 1), cpi = as.numeric(cpi)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cpi)) %>% select(cpi_month, cpi)
}
cpi_nat <- map(cpi_sheets, ~ parse_cpi_national(params$cpi_path, .x)) %>%
  list_rbind() %>% distinct(cpi_month, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% arrange(cpi_month)

4.4.1 Validation: chain continuity at sheet junctions

The workbooks are supplied as a single chained series (2018 = 100). If that is true, the implied month-on-month log change at each sheet junction (Dec 2005 → Jan 2006, Dec 2017 → Jan 2018) should look like ordinary monthly inflation. Junction changes above 5% in absolute value stop the document.

junctions <- as.Date(c("2006-01-01", "2018-01-01"))

continuity <- cpi_long %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>%
  arrange(cpi_month, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(mom_log = log(cpi) - log(lag(cpi))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(cpi_month %in% junctions) %>%
  select(region_wb, cpi_month, mom_log)

continuity %>%
  mutate(mom_pct = 100 * (exp(mom_log) - 1)) %>%
  select(-mom_log) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cpi_month, values_from = mom_pct) %>%
  kt("Implied month-on-month inflation (%) across CPI sheet junctions -- values should look like ordinary monthly inflation", digits = 2)

4.4.2 Deflators (N3) and the configuration-difference table

# (N3): defl_{r,m} = CPI_{r,m} / mean(CPI_{r, months of 2018});
#       real_x = x / defl. If the file is exactly 2018-based, the base
#       means printed below are ~100 and the rebasing is an identity.
cpi_base <- cpi_long %>%
  filter(year(cpi_month) == BASE_YEAR) %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>%
  summarise(cpi_base_2018 = mean(cpi), .groups = "drop")

# Compact verification instead of a 17-row table: if the workbook is truly
# 2018-based, every regional 2018 mean is ~100.
cat(sprintf("Region 2018 mean CPI across lineages: min %.2f, max %.2f %s\n",
            min(cpi_base$cpi_base_2018), max(cpi_base$cpi_base_2018),
            if (all(abs(cpi_base$cpi_base_2018 - 100) < 2))
              "-- consistent with a 2018=100 base; rebasing is an identity."
            else
              "-- NOT all ~100; the explicit rebasing below is doing real work."))
## Region 2018 mean CPI across lineages: min 99.98, max 100.01 -- consistent with a 2018=100 base; rebasing is an identity.
cpi_defl <- cpi_long %>%
  left_join(cpi_base, by = "region_wb") %>%
  mutate(defl = cpi / cpi_base_2018)

# Configuration difference: current PSA (NIR-configured) VI/VII vs the
# pre-NIR series used here, latest common month. Reference only.
cpi_nir_2018 <- parse_cpi_sheet(params$cpi_nir_path, "2018-") %>%
  filter(region_wb %in% c("VI", "VII"))
cfg_diff <- cpi_nir_2018 %>%
  rename(cpi_nir_cfg = cpi) %>%
  inner_join(cpi_long %>% rename(cpi_pre_nir = cpi),
             by = c("region_wb", "cpi_month")) %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% slice_max(cpi_month, n = 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cpi_nir_cfg / cpi_pre_nir - 1))
kt(cfg_diff, "Regions VI/VII: current PSA (Negros-excluding) vs pre-NIR (Negros-including) CPI, latest common month. The pre-NIR series is the one used throughout, matching lineage geography.", digits = 2)

4.5 Poverty thresholds: vintages, conversion, and monthly projection

PovertyThresholds.xlsx carries annual per-capita thresholds by region for five methodology vintages at (mostly) triennial survey years. The rules implemented here, per the design discussion:

  • Series in force (later vintage preferred at overlaps, but the pre-NIR-geography vintage retained through 2021 for consistency with the lineage boundaries): 2003 ← 2000-2006; 2006, 2009, 2012 ← 2006-2015; 2015, 2018, 2021 ← 2015-2021 (No NIR); 2023 ← 2018-2023 (With NIR).
  • The 2023 (with-NIR) VI/VII values exclude Negros while our VI/VII lineages include it — a documented approximation for 2023+ (the NIR row is not separately usable at lineage level). Overlap ratios below show the size of every vintage/geography seam.
  • (N9) conversion to a daily-wage equivalent, then (N10) CPI projection to monthly frequency, with linear interpolation as sensitivity.
pt_raw <- read_excel(params$pt_path, sheet = "Thresholds")

pt_region_map <- c(
  "NCR" = "NCR", "CAR" = "CAR",
  "Region I - Ilocos" = "I", "Region II - Cagayan Valley" = "II",
  "Region III - Central Luzon" = "III",
  "Region IVA - CALABARZON" = "IV-A", "Region IVB - MIMAROPA" = "IV-B",
  "Region V - Bicol" = "V", "Region VI - Western Visayas" = "VI",
  "Region VII - Central Visayas" = "VII",
  "Region VIII - Eastern Visayas" = "VIII",
  "Region IX - Zamboanga Peninsula" = "IX",
  "Region X - Northern Mindanao" = "X",
  "Region XI - Davao" = "XI", "Region XII - SOCCSKSARGEN" = "XII",
  "Region XIII - Caraga" = "XIII",
  "ARMM" = "ARMM-BARMM", "BARMM" = "ARMM-BARMM"
)

pt_long <- pt_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Series, Region), names_to = "pt_year",
               values_to = "pt_percap_ann") %>%
  mutate(pt_year = as.integer(pt_year)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pt_percap_ann), Region %in% names(pt_region_map)) %>%
  mutate(region_wb = factor(pt_region_map[Region], levels = REGION_ORDER))

# Series-in-force rule
series_in_force <- tribble(
  ~pt_year, ~Series,
  2003, "2000-2006",
  2006, "2006-2015", 2009, "2006-2015", 2012, "2006-2015",
  2015, "2015-2021 (No NIR)", 2018, "2015-2021 (No NIR)",
  2021, "2015-2021 (No NIR)",
  2023, "2018-2023 (With NIR)"
)

pt_inforce <- pt_long %>%
  inner_join(series_in_force, by = c("pt_year", "Series")) %>%
  select(region_wb, pt_year, pt_percap_ann) %>%
  arrange(region_wb, pt_year)

stopifnot("Every lineage must have every in-force threshold year" =
  nrow(pt_inforce) == length(REGION_ORDER) * nrow(series_in_force))

4.5.1 Validation: vintage overlap ratios

# Where two vintages publish the same (region, year), their ratio measures
# the methodology / geography revision at that seam.
pt_overlap <- pt_long %>%
  group_by(region_wb, pt_year) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(Series, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(series_pair = paste(Series, collapse = "  vs  "),
            ratio_later_over_earlier = pt_percap_ann[n()] / pt_percap_ann[1],
            .groups = "drop")

pt_overlap %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pt_year, values_from = ratio_later_over_earlier,
              id_cols = region_wb) %>%

4.5.2 Conversion (N9) and monthly projection (N10)

# (N9): PT_wage(r, y) = PT_percap_ann(r, y) * FAMILY_SIZE / (EARNERS * FACTOR_DAYS)
pt_wage_y <- pt_inforce %>%
  mutate(pt_wage_daily     = pt_percap_ann * FAMILY_SIZE / (EARNERS * FACTOR_DAYS),
         pt_wage_daily_365 = pt_percap_ann * FAMILY_SIZE / (EARNERS * FACTOR_DAYS_ALT))

# Annual-mean CPI per (lineage, year) -- the denominator of (N10)
cpi_ann <- cpi_defl %>%
  group_by(region_wb, yr = year(cpi_month)) %>%
  summarise(cpi_ann = mean(cpi), .groups = "drop")

# (N10): PT_wage(r, m) = PT_wage(r, y*) * CPI(r, m) / CPI_ann(r, y*),
#        y* = max{ threshold years <= year(m) }.
pt_monthly <- cpi_defl %>%
  select(region_wb, cpi_month, cpi) %>%
  mutate(yr = year(cpi_month)) %>%
  filter(yr >= 2004) %>%
  left_join(
    pt_wage_y %>% rename(pt_anchor_year = pt_year),
    by = "region_wb", relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(pt_anchor_year <= yr) %>%
  group_by(region_wb, cpi_month) %>%
  slice_max(pt_anchor_year, n = 1) %>%      # y* = latest anchor not after m
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(cpi_ann, by = c("region_wb", "pt_anchor_year" = "yr")) %>%
  mutate(pt_wage_m     = pt_wage_daily     * cpi / cpi_ann,
         pt_wage_m_365 = pt_wage_daily_365 * cpi / cpi_ann) %>%
  select(region_wb, cpi_month, pt_anchor_year, pt_wage_m, pt_wage_m_365)

# Sensitivity: LINEAR interpolation in nominal levels between survey-year
# anchors placed at July 1 of each survey year; no extrapolation past the
# last anchor. approx(..., rule = 1) returns NA outside the anchor range.
pt_linear <- pt_wage_y %>%
  mutate(anchor_date = make_date(pt_year, 7, 1)) %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>%
  reframe({
    grid <- seq(make_date(2004, 1, 1), make_date(2025, 6, 1), by = "month")
    tibble(cpi_month = grid,
           pt_wage_linear = approx(x = as.numeric(anchor_date),
                                   y = pt_wage_daily,
                                   xout = as.numeric(grid), rule = 1)$y)
  })

pt_monthly <- pt_monthly %>%
  left_join(pt_linear, by = c("region_wb", "cpi_month"))

4.5.3 The spatial price index \(\theta_r\) (N13)

This is the primary analytic use of the poverty thresholds in this document: their 2018 cross-region ratios index price levels across regions (which the CPI cannot), so that a real ₱25 means the same purchasing power everywhere once combined with the CPI’s within-region time indexing. The wage-adequacy statistics later on are auxiliary.

# (N13): theta_r = PT^pc_{r,2018} / PT^pc_{NCR,2018}  (No-NIR vintage).
# Family-size / earner / factor-day constants cancel in the ratio.
theta_tbl <- pt_inforce %>%
  filter(pt_year == 2018) %>%
  transmute(region_wb,
            theta = pt_percap_ann / pt_percap_ann[region_wb == SPATIAL_BASE])
stopifnot(nrow(theta_tbl) == length(REGION_ORDER),
          abs(theta_tbl$theta[theta_tbl$region_wb == SPATIAL_BASE] - 1) < 1e-12)

theta_tbl %>%
  mutate(band_width_local_php = AT_MW_BAND_PHP_REAL * theta) %>%
  kt(sprintf("Spatial price index theta (base: %s = 1) and the local real-2018-peso width of the 'P25' band in each region", SPATIAL_BASE), digits = 3)

# Overlay for four contrasting lineages: where CPI projection and linear
# interpolation diverge is exactly where inflation deviated from the
# between-survey trend (2018, 2022-23 spikes).
pt_monthly %>%
  filter(region_wb %in% c("NCR", "IV-A", "VIII", "ARMM-BARMM")) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(pt_wage_m, pt_wage_linear),
               names_to = "method", values_to = "pt") %>%
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         pt_wage_m = "CPI projection (headline, N10)",
                         pt_wage_linear = "Linear interpolation (sensitivity)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(cpi_month, pt, colour = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2c7bb6", "#d7191c")) +
  labs(title = "Poverty-threshold daily-wage equivalent: projection method comparison",
       subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
         "PT_wage = annual per-capita threshold x %d / (%d earner x %d factor days), then projected monthly. Divergence marks inflation deviating from the between-survey trend.",
         FAMILY_SIZE, EARNERS, FACTOR_DAYS)),
       x = NULL, y = "PHP per day (nominal)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The two projection methods agree wherever inflation tracked its between-survey trend and split apart where it did not (most visibly around the 2018 and 2022–23 inflation episodes, where the CPI projection lifts the threshold immediately while linear interpolation smooths through). The gap between the lines is the measurement uncertainty introduced by projecting a triennial statistic to monthly frequency — modest relative to the threshold level, but not zero, which is why both methods are carried.

4.6 Merge: LFS × wage orders × CPI × poverty thresholds

Merge keys are (lineage, reference month) throughout; the wage-order side enters through the as-of function (N2) evaluated at ref_date, the CPI and poverty sides join on the calendar month of ref_date.

lfs <- lfs %>%
  mutate(
    mw_tot_max = assign_mw_lineage(ref_date, region_wb, "total_max"),
    mw_tot_min = assign_mw_lineage(ref_date, region_wb, "total_min"),
    mw_bas_max = assign_mw_lineage(ref_date, region_wb, "basic_max"),
    mw_bas_min = assign_mw_lineage(ref_date, region_wb, "basic_min")
  ) %>%
  left_join(cpi_defl %>% select(region_wb, cpi_month, defl),
            by = c("region_wb", "ref_date" = "cpi_month")) %>%
  left_join(pt_monthly %>% select(region_wb, cpi_month, pt_wage_m,
                                  pt_wage_m_365, pt_wage_linear),
            by = c("region_wb", "ref_date" = "cpi_month")) %>%
  left_join(theta_tbl, by = "region_wb")   # spatial index (N13)

merge_diag <- lfs %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            pct_mw_na   = 100 * mean(is.na(mw_tot_max)),
            pct_defl_na = 100 * mean(is.na(defl)),
            pct_pt_na   = 100 * mean(is.na(pt_wage_m)),
            pct_theta_na = 100 * mean(is.na(theta)))
kt(merge_diag, "Merge diagnostics: share of LFS rows lacking an assigned MW / deflator / poverty wage (all should be 0)", digits = 3)
Merge diagnostics: share of LFS rows lacking an assigned MW / deflator / poverty wage (all should be 0)

stopifnot(merge_diag$pct_mw_na == 0, merge_diag$pct_defl_na == 0)

5 Sample Construction: the A / B / C Cascade

Three nested samples, per the agreed convention. Only Sample C feeds the Kaitz, compliance-partition, bunching, and wage-bin sections; Samples A and B appear in the descriptive trends and the reconciliation.

  • Sample A (naive): employed, positive reported daily basic pay, age 15–64 — every pay report regardless of class or industry.
  • Sample B (wage workers): A ∩ class_label ∈ {Private Establishment, Government/GOCC, Private Household} — the NCR-PoC-comparable universe.
  • Sample C (covered sector): B ∩ class_label = Private Establishment ∩ non-agriculture (ind_section ≠ "A", non-missing) — the universe the non-agriculture wage orders actually govern (less the establishment-size and apprentice exemptions the LFS cannot observe; see the Limitations register).
base <- lfs %>%
  mutate(pay_ok = !is.na(basic_pay_php) & basic_pay_php > 0,
         age_ok = age_years >= 15 & age_years <= 64,
         w_ok   = !is.na(weight) & weight > 0)

sample_A <- base %>% filter(employed == 1, pay_ok, age_ok, w_ok)
sample_B <- sample_A %>% filter(class_label %in% WAGE_CLASS_LABELS)
sample_C <- sample_B %>% filter(class_label == COVERED_CLASS,
                                !is.na(ind_section), ind_section != "A")

waterfall <- tribble(
  ~step, ~restriction, ~n_unwt, ~pop_wt,
  "0", "All LFS person-quarters (mapped to a lineage)",
       nrow(base), sum(base$weight, na.rm = TRUE),
  "A", "Employed, positive daily basic pay, age 15-64, valid weight",
       nrow(sample_A), sum(sample_A$weight),
  "B", "A and wage-worker class (Priv. Est. / Gov't / Priv. HH)",
       nrow(sample_B), sum(sample_B$weight),
  "C", "B and Private Establishment only, non-agriculture",
       nrow(sample_C), sum(sample_C$weight)
) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_A_unwt = 100 * n_unwt / n_unwt[step == "A"],
         pop_wt_m = pop_wt / 1e6)

waterfall %>% select(-pop_wt) %>%
  kt("Sample-construction waterfall (pooled 2004-2025). pop_wt_m = weighted person-quarters, millions.",
     digits = c(NA, NA, 0, 1, 1), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

6 The Master Quarterly Panel

All bindingness statistics are computed once, here, into a single lineage × quarter panel (bind_qtr) plus its person-level-pooled national counterpart (bind_nat, per N11). Every downstream bindingness chart reads from these two tables, so a formula is implemented in exactly one place.

# Per (lineage, quarter) on Sample C -- formulas N1, N4, N5, N6:
#   percentiles: Q(p) via weighted_quantile (N1)
#   kaitz_med   = mw_tot_max / Q(0.50)                     (N4)
#   kaitz_mean  = mw_tot_max / weighted mean               (N4)
#   F_at_below  = Fhat(mw_tot_max)          [w <= MW, weak] (N4)
#   B_max/B_min = Pr[w < mw_tot_max] / Pr[w < mw_tot_min]  (N5, strict)
#   partition   = below (w < .95 MW) / at (|w/MW-1|<=.05) / above (N6)
#   at_real25s  = |real w - real MW| <= 25 * theta_r        (N6 sensitivity,
#                 spatially indexed per N13; identical to the PoC in NCR)
#   B_bas_max   = Pr[w < mw_bas_max]  (basic-rate sensitivity, Robustness section)
#   below_pt    = Pr[w < PT_wage_m]                         (N9/N10)
bind_qtr <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(real_pay = basic_pay_php / defl,
         real_mw  = mw_tot_max   / defl) %>%
  group_by(region_wb, year, quarter, ref_date,
           mw_tot_max, mw_tot_min, mw_bas_max, pt_wage_m, theta) %>%
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    pop_wt = sum(weight),
    p05 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.05),
    p10 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.10),
    p25 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.25),
    p50 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.50),
    p75 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.75),
    p90 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.90),
    mean_pay      = wmean(basic_pay_php, weight),
    p50_real      = weighted_quantile(real_pay, weight, 0.50),
    mean_pay_real = wmean(real_pay, weight),
    F_at_below    = wshare(basic_pay_php <= mw_tot_max, weight),
    B_max         = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_max, weight),
    B_min         = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_min, weight),
    B_bas_max     = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_bas_max, weight),
    part_below    = wshare(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1 < -AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    part_at       = wshare(abs(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1) <= AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    part_above    = wshare(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1 >  AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    at_real25s    = wshare(abs(real_pay - real_mw) <= AT_MW_BAND_PHP_REAL * theta,
                           weight),
    below_pt      = wshare(basic_pay_php < pt_wage_m, weight),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(kaitz_med    = mw_tot_max / p50,
         kaitz_mean   = mw_tot_max / mean_pay,
         kaitz_med_min = mw_tot_min / p50,
         low_n        = n < MIN_CELL_N)

# Real MW and real poverty wage at the cell level: divide by the same
# regional deflator (N3) used for wages.
bind_qtr <- bind_qtr %>%
  left_join(cpi_defl %>% select(region_wb, cpi_month, defl),
            by = c("region_wb", "ref_date" = "cpi_month")) %>%
  mutate(mw_real = mw_tot_max / defl,
         pt_real = pt_wage_m / defl)

# Partition must sum to 1 exactly (each obs in exactly one N6 class)
stopifnot(max(abs(bind_qtr$part_below + bind_qtr$part_at +
                  bind_qtr$part_above - 1), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-9)

# National pooled panel (N11): person-level against own regional floor
bind_nat <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(real_pay = basic_pay_php / defl,
         real_mw  = mw_tot_max / defl) %>%
  group_by(year, quarter, ref_date) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(), pop_wt = sum(weight),
    p10 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.10),
    p50 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.50),
    p90 = weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.90),
    p50_real   = weighted_quantile(real_pay, weight, 0.50),
    mean_real  = wmean(real_pay, weight),
    F_at_below = wshare(basic_pay_php <= mw_tot_max, weight),
    B_max      = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_max, weight),
    B_min      = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_min, weight),
    B_bas_max  = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_bas_max, weight),
    part_below = wshare(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1 < -AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    part_at    = wshare(abs(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1) <= AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    part_above = wshare(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1 >  AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
    at_real25s = wshare(abs(real_pay - real_mw) <= AT_MW_BAND_PHP_REAL * theta,
                        weight),
    below_pt   = wshare(basic_pay_php < pt_wage_m, weight),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# National Kaitz (N11): covered-employment-weighted mean of regional Kaitz,
# with the cross-region min-max range.
kaitz_nat <- bind_qtr %>%
  group_by(year, quarter, ref_date) %>%
  summarise(kaitz_nat  = sum(pop_wt * kaitz_med) / sum(pop_wt),
            kaitz_min  = min(kaitz_med),
            kaitz_max  = max(kaitz_med), .groups = "drop")

7 Wage Levels: Mean and Median Trends

Formula note. Real series deflate by the regional CPI (N3); the national real median is the pooled weighted median of regionally-deflated wages — i.e., each peso is converted to 2018 purchasing power in its own region before pooling.

bind_nat %>%
  select(ref_date, `Median (real 2018 PHP)` = p50_real,
         `Mean (real 2018 PHP)` = mean_real) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ref_date) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#d7191c", "#2c7bb6")) +
  labs(title = "National real daily basic pay, covered sector (Sample C)",
       subtitle = "Weighted mean and median, regional-CPI-deflated to 2018 PHP, pooled across lineages",
       x = NULL, y = "2018 PHP per day", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. Between the first and last full year of the sample, the national real median daily basic pay in the covered sector moved from ₱371 to ₱426 (2018 PHP), a cumulative +15% over two decades. The mean sitting above the median reflects right skew, as in any wage distribution. This chart shows purchasing-power trends only; it says nothing by itself about why they moved.

bind_qtr %>%
  select(region_wb, ref_date, p50_real, mw_real, pt_real) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(region_wb, ref_date)) %>%
  mutate(name = recode(name,
                       p50_real = "Median wage",
                       mw_real  = "Minimum wage (total_max)",
                       pt_real  = "Poverty wage (family of 5, 1 earner)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Median wage" = "grey25",
                                 "Minimum wage (total_max)" = "#2c7bb6",
                                 "Poverty wage (family of 5, 1 earner)" = "#d7191c")) +
  labs(title = "Real median wage vs. the wage floor vs. the poverty wage, by lineage",
       subtitle = "All series in 2018 PHP per day, regional CPI deflators. Shared y-scale for cross-region comparability.",
       x = NULL, y = "2018 PHP per day", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The striking structural fact is how close the blue floor line runs to the grey median in most lineages — in 10 of 17 lineages the latest-quarter real floor sits at or above the covered-sector real median. The red poverty-wage line adds the adequacy anchor: where blue runs below red, even full compliance at the floor would not support the reference family. Co-movement of the three lines is expected by construction (all deflated by the same regional CPI) and is not evidence of causation in any direction.

8 Bindingness: The Kaitz Index

Formulas (N4, N11). \(K^{med}_{r,t} = MW^{tot,max}_{r,t} / Q_{r,t}(0.5)\); the dashed companion uses \(MW^{tot,min}\), so the vertical gap between the two lines is the pure multi-rate-interval effect on measured bindingness.

ggplot(kaitz_nat, aes(ref_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = kaitz_min, ymax = kaitz_max),
              fill = "#2c7bb6", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = kaitz_nat), colour = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 1.0), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey45") +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2004-06-01"), y = 1.02,
           label = "1.0 - MW = median", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2004-06-01"), y = 0.52,
           label = "0.5 - int'l 'meaningfully binding'", hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "National Kaitz index (covered-employment-weighted mean of regional indices)",
       subtitle = "Shaded band = cross-region min-max range of regional Kaitz(median) each quarter",
       x = NULL, y = "Kaitz index (MW / median)")

Reading. The latest national Kaitz index is 0.96, with regional indices spanning 0.88–1.20 in that quarter. Values in this neighbourhood are extraordinary by international standards — rich-country minimum wages typically sit near 0.5 of the median — and mean the Philippine floor is set at the centre of the covered wage distribution, not its tail. A high Kaitz signals where the floor is aimed; it does not by itself say whether the floor is complied with or what it does to employment.

bind_qtr %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = kaitz_med, colour = "MW(total_max) / median"), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = kaitz_med_min, colour = "MW(total_min) / median"),
            linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey45") +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("MW(total_max) / median" = "#2c7bb6",
                                 "MW(total_min) / median" = "#fdae61")) +
  labs(title = "Kaitz index by wage-board lineage",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Solid = headline (total_max numerator); dashed = total_min numerator. The gap is the multi-rate interval. Dotted line: MW equal to the covered-sector median."),
       x = NULL, y = "Kaitz index", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. Bindingness is high everywhere but not uniform: the spread between lineages, and within each panel the gap between the solid (total_max) and dashed (total_min) lines, shows how much of measured bindingness depends on which statutory rate is used as the ruler. Panels where the two lines separate widely are exactly the multi-rate boards flagged in the wage-order section; treat any single-line Kaitz quote for those regions with suspicion.

  select(region_wb, year, kaitz_med) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = kaitz_med) %>%
  kt("Kaitz(median) at Q2 of selected years, by lineage (Sample C)", digits = 2)

9 The Compliance Partition and the Noncompliance Interval

Formulas. The stacked partition is (N6): below (\(w < 0.95\,MW\)), at (\(|w/MW - 1| \le 0.05\)), above (\(w > 1.05\,MW\)), with \(MW = MW^{tot,max}\). The interval chart is (N5): strict shares \(B^{max} = \Pr[w < MW^{tot,max}]\) and \(B^{min} = \Pr[w < MW^{tot,min}]\); true noncompliance lies inside the ribbon (up to the coverage caveats in the Limitations register).

bind_nat %>%
  select(ref_date, Below = part_below, At = part_at, Above = part_above) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ref_date, names_to = "band", values_to = "share") %>%
  mutate(band = factor(band, levels = c("Above", "At", "Below"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, share, fill = band)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Above = "#a6d96a", At = "#fdae61", Below = "#d7191c")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "National compliance partition, covered sector",
       subtitle = sprintf("Below / at / above the applicable regional MW (total_max), at-band = +/-%d%% (N6)", 100 * AT_MW_BAND_PCT),
       x = NULL, y = "share of covered wage employment", fill = NULL)

Reading. In the latest quarter, 27% of covered wage employment is paid more than 5% below the applicable floor, 25% within ±5% of it, and 48% above. The sawtooth texture is mechanical: each wage order instantly reclassifies workers relative to a higher ruler, after which nominal wage growth walks them back up. The below-band share bundles genuine noncompliance with lawful exemptions and rate-interval ambiguity — it is an upper-bound-flavoured measure, not a violation rate.

bind_qtr %>%
  select(region_wb, ref_date, Below = part_below, At = part_at, Above = part_above) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(region_wb, ref_date), names_to = "band", values_to = "share") %>%
  mutate(band = factor(band, levels = c("Above", "At", "Below"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, share, fill = band)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Above = "#a6d96a", At = "#fdae61", Below = "#d7191c")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Compliance partition by lineage", x = NULL,
       y = "share of covered wage employment", fill = NULL)

Reading. The same partition by lineage shows the compliance landscape is regional: some panels are dominated by the green above-band, others carry persistently large red below-band shares. Because the ±5% band is scale-invariant, these differences are not artifacts of wage levels — they reflect real differences in the floor’s position in each region’s distribution and in adherence to it. Cross-panel level differences are the motivation for reporting every national statistic alongside its facets.

bind_qtr %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = B_min, ymax = B_max), fill = "#d7191c", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = B_max), colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_line(aes(y = B_min), colour = "#7f0000", linewidth = 0.45, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Strict noncompliance interval by lineage (N5)",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Solid = share below total_max (upper bound); dashed = share below total_min (definite subminimum pay). True noncompliance lies inside the ribbon; establishment-size and apprentice exemptions (unobserved) can only shrink it further."),
       x = NULL, y = "share of covered wage employment")

Reading. The ribbon is the honest answer to “what share of workers is paid below the minimum wage?” — it depends on which minimum. The lower dashed line (below every applicable rate) is definite sub-minimum pay; the ribbon width is classification ambiguity from multi-rate boards, reaching 38 percentage points at its widest lineage-quarter. Unobserved exemptions (small retail, apprentices, BMBEs) can only shrink true noncompliance further below the upper line.

9.1 Reference modules: Government and Private Household (kasambahay)

These two classes are outside the covered sector: government pay is set by the Salary Standardization Law, and domestic workers fall under the Kasambahay Law’s separate (much lower) floor. Their strict share below the regional non-agriculture total_max is shown as context, not as a noncompliance estimate.

ref_mod <- sample_B %>%
  filter(class_label != COVERED_CLASS) %>%
  group_by(class_label, ref_date) %>%
  summarise(B_max = wshare(basic_pay_php < mw_tot_max, weight),
            .groups = "drop")

bind_nat %>% transmute(class_label = "Private Establishment (covered, non-agri)",
                       ref_date, B_max) %>%
  bind_rows(ref_mod) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, B_max, colour = class_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Private Establishment (covered, non-agri)" = "#2c7bb6",
                                 "Government/GOCC" = "#5e3c99",
                                 "Private Household" = "#e66101")) +
  labs(title = "Share paid below the regional non-agriculture floor, by worker class (national)",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Government and Private Household are NOT covered by the non-agriculture wage orders (SSL and Kasambahay Law respectively); their series are context, not noncompliance."),
       x = NULL, y = "share below regional total_max", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The two reference series confirm the sample design rather than measure violations: Private Household workers sit overwhelmingly below the non-agriculture floor because the Kasambahay Law sets them a separate, much lower one, and Government pay follows the SSL. Their divergence from the covered-sector line is a coverage boundary, and it is why both classes are excluded from every compliance statistic in this document.

10 Auxiliary: The Poverty-Wage Adequacy Benchmark

Role in this document. The poverty thresholds’ primary job here is the N13 spatial index — making real-peso bands comparable across regions. This section is the auxiliary use: the thresholds as a wage-adequacy benchmark in their own right. It is retained because it is cheap and policy-legible, but nothing downstream depends on it.

Disclaimer (stated once, meant everywhere): a wage below \(PT^{wage}_{r,m}\) is a wage-adequacy statistic — the daily basic pay is insufficient for a hypothetical single-earner family of five at the poverty line. It is not a poverty rate: actual household poverty depends on household size, number of earners, and non-wage income, none of which this statistic conditions on.

# Ratio (N2, N9, N10): MW^{tot,max}_{r,m} / PT_wage_{r,m}. Values >= 1 mean
# a full factor-day year at the floor clears the poverty line for a
# family of five on one earner.
bind_qtr %>%
  mutate(mw_over_pt = mw_tot_max / pt_wage_m) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, mw_over_pt)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(colour = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 0.55) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Does a full year at the minimum wage clear the poverty line?",
       subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
         "MW(total_max) / PT_wage, where PT_wage = annual per-capita threshold x %d / (%d x %d factor days), CPI-projected monthly (N10). Dotted line = exactly clears the line.",
         FAMILY_SIZE, EARNERS, FACTOR_DAYS)),
       x = NULL, y = "MW / poverty wage")

Reading. In the latest quarter the floor clears the family-of-five poverty wage in 1 of 17 lineages. The within-panel sawtooth repeats the erosion cycle: each order lifts the ratio, inflation grinds it back down. Remember the maintained assumptions — one earner, family of five, 313 paid days — before quoting any single ratio; the level shifts proportionally under other conventions, though the time pattern does not.

bind_nat %>%
  select(ref_date, `below poverty wage` = below_pt,
         `below MW (strict, total_max)` = B_max) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ref_date) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#d7191c", "#2c7bb6")) +
  labs(title = "National shares below the poverty wage and below the minimum wage (covered sector)",
       subtitle = "Wage-adequacy measure, NOT a poverty rate (see disclaimer). Person-level pooling against own regional thresholds (N11).",
       x = NULL, y = "share of covered wage employment", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. In the latest quarter 57% of covered wage workers earn below the poverty wage and 37% below the highest applicable floor; the two series moving together reflects the floor and the threshold occupying the same neighbourhood of the distribution. Per the standing disclaimer, the red series is wage adequacy for a hypothetical household, not a poverty headcount — multi-earner households routinely escape poverty on individually sub-threshold wages.

# Divisor sensitivity (N9): factor-days 313 (headline) vs calendar 365.
# The two differ by the fixed ratio 365/313 = 1.166; the table shows the
# effect on the latest-quarter national share below the poverty wage.
alt <- sample_C %>%
  filter(ref_date == max(ref_date)) %>%
  summarise(
    `share below PT (313 factor days)` = wshare(basic_pay_php < pt_wage_m, weight),
    `share below PT (365 calendar days)` = wshare(basic_pay_php < pt_wage_m_365, weight),
    `share below PT (linear interpolation)` = wshare(basic_pay_php < pt_wage_linear, weight))
latest_d <- max(sample_C$ref_date)
kt(alt, sprintf("Poverty-wage sensitivity, latest quarter (%d Q%d): divisor convention and projection method",
                year(latest_d), quarter(latest_d)), digits = 3)
Poverty-wage sensitivity, latest quarter (2025 Q2): divisor convention and projection method
share below PT (313 factor days) share below PT (365 calendar days) share below PT (linear interpolation)

11 Heaping Diagnostics

Formula (N12). \(H_d = \Pr_\omega[w_i \bmod d = 0]\), weighted, Sample C. Heaping is the identification threat for bunching: a spike at a round MW is confounded with round-number reporting; a spike at an off-round MW is not.

heap_period <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(subper = paste0(floor(year / 5) * 5, "-", floor(year / 5) * 5 + 4)) %>%
  group_by(subper) %>%
  summarise(
    div_5   = 100 * wshare(basic_pay_php %% 5   == 0, weight),   # (N12), d = 5
    div_10  = 100 * wshare(basic_pay_php %% 10  == 0, weight),   # d = 10
    div_50  = 100 * wshare(basic_pay_php %% 50  == 0, weight),   # d = 50
    div_100 = 100 * wshare(basic_pay_php %% 100 == 0, weight),   # d = 100
    n = n(), .groups = "drop")
kt(heap_period, "Weighted share of wage reports divisible by 5 / 10 / 50 / 100 PHP, by 5-year subperiod (Sample C, national)", digits = 1)

11.1 Wage-order roundness by lineage

# An order is "off-round" if its total_max is NOT divisible by 50 -- at such
# rates, digit heaping cannot mechanically manufacture a spike at the floor.
roundness <- mw_lineage %>%
  filter(effectivity_date >= as.Date("2004-01-01")) %>%
  mutate(round50 = total_max %% 50 == 0) %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>%
  summarise(n_orders = n(), n_round50 = sum(round50),
            pct_off_round = 100 * mean(!round50), .groups = "drop")

qtr_round <- qtr_grid %>%
