12 Bunching at the Floor

12.1 Pooled log-distance histogram

Formula (N7). Weighted share per 0.025-log-point bin of \(\log w_i - \log MW_{r(i)}(d_{t(i)})\), each worker against their own contemporaneous regional floor; pooled across all lineages and quarters, then also faceted by lineage.

bunch <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(logdist = log(basic_pay_php) - log(mw_tot_max)) %>%
  filter(abs(logdist) <= LOG_BIN_LIM) %>%
  mutate(bin = floor(logdist / LOG_BIN_H) * LOG_BIN_H)

bunch_nat <- bunch %>%
  group_by(bin) %>% summarise(w = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share = w / sum(w))

ggplot(bunch_nat, aes(bin + LOG_BIN_H / 2, share)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7bb6", width = LOG_BIN_H * 0.92) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Pooled wage distribution in log distance to the own-region minimum wage (N7)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Sample C, all lineages and quarters pooled; bin width %.3f log points (~%.1f%% of MW). Red line = the floor.", LOG_BIN_H, 100 * LOG_BIN_H),
       x = "log(wage) - log(regional MW, total_max)", y = "weighted share")

Reading. The pooled distribution shows visible mass concentration at and just below each worker’s own contemporaneous floor (the red line), with the sub-floor shoulder confirming that the floor truncates pay-setting imperfectly. Some of the spike at zero is genuine floor-referenced pay-setting and some is round-number reporting landing on round wage orders — the heaping section and the off-round split below exist precisely because this chart alone cannot separate the two.

bunch %>%
  group_by(region_wb, bin) %>% summarise(w = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% mutate(share = w / sum(w)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(bin + LOG_BIN_H / 2, share)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7bb6", width = LOG_BIN_H * 0.92) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Log-distance wage distributions by lineage (pooled over quarters)",
       x = "log(wage) - log(regional MW)", y = "weighted share")

Reading. Bunching at the own-region floor appears in every lineage, which is itself informative: floor-referenced pay-setting is a national phenomenon, not an NCR one. Differences in spike height and sub-floor shoulder across panels track the regional compliance differences seen in the partition facets. Panel shapes, not levels, are the comparable object here since each panel is normalised within its own lineage.

12.2 Off-round vs. round region-quarters

# At-band share (N6, +/-5%) over time, splitting region-quarters by whether
# the prevailing total_max is divisible by 50. If the at-MW spike were pure
# digit heaping, the off-round series would sit near zero.
at_by_round <- sample_C %>%
  left_join(qtr_round, by = c("region_wb", "ref_date")) %>%
  mutate(grp = if_else(mw_round50, "Round MW (divisible by 50)",
                       "Off-round MW")) %>%
  group_by(ref_date, grp) %>%
  summarise(at5 = wshare(abs(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1) <= AT_MW_BAND_PCT,
                         weight), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(at_by_round, aes(ref_date, at5, colour = grp)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Off-round MW" = "#2c7bb6",
                                 "Round MW (divisible by 50)" = "#fdae61")) +
  labs(title = "Share within +/-5% of the floor: off-round vs round minimum wages",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Region-quarters grouped by whether the prevailing total_max is divisible by 50. Bunching at off-round floors cannot be manufactured by round-number reporting; the off-round series is the cleaner signal of policy-linked pay-setting."),
       x = NULL, y = "share within +/-5% of MW", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. This is the cleanest evidence that bunching is real: in region-quarters where the prevailing floor is not a round number, 25% of covered workers still sit within ±5% of it in the latest quarter. Digit heaping cannot manufacture a spike at ₱517; only pay-setting that references the wage order can. The gap between the two lines bounds how much of the round-MW at-share is a reporting artifact.

13 The Region × Quarter × ₱25 Wage-Bin Panel (Saved Artifact)

Formula (N8). Left-closed ₱25 bins of \((w_i - MW^{tot,max}_{r}(d_t))\) in nominal pesos, from −300 to +600; per \((r, t, b)\) the panel stores the unweighted count, summed weight, and weighted within-cell share. This is design (a) of the PoC’s feasibility matrix — the input any stacked-DiD / event-study analysis would consume — saved to Output/.

bin_breaks <- seq(BIN_LO, BIN_HI + BIN_PHP, by = BIN_PHP)

bin_panel <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(rel = basic_pay_php - mw_tot_max,
         bin = if_else(rel >= BIN_LO & rel < BIN_HI + BIN_PHP,
                       floor(rel / BIN_PHP) * BIN_PHP, NA_real_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bin)) %>%
  group_by(region_wb, year, quarter, ref_date, mw_tot_max, bin) %>%
  summarise(n_unwt = n(), w_sum = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(region_wb, ref_date) %>%
  mutate(share_wt = w_sum / sum(w_sum)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # complete the grid so zero-mass bins exist explicitly (a Cengiz-style
  # averaging requirement flagged in the PoC)
  complete(nesting(region_wb, year, quarter, ref_date, mw_tot_max),
           bin = head(bin_breaks, -1),
           fill = list(n_unwt = 0L, w_sum = 0, share_wt = 0))

write_rds(bin_panel, "Output/wage_bin_panel_region_quarter.rds")
write_csv(bin_panel, "Output/wage_bin_panel_region_quarter.csv")
cat("Saved wage-bin panel:",
    comma(nrow(bin_panel)), "rows (",
    n_distinct(bin_panel$region_wb), "lineages x",
    n_distinct(bin_panel$ref_date), "quarters x",
    length(bin_breaks) - 1, "bins )\n")
## Saved wage-bin panel: 54,057 rows ( 17 lineages x 86 quarters x 37 bins )
# Preview: national average bin shares, first 4 vs latest 4 sample years.
bin_panel %>%
  mutate(era = case_when(year <= 2007 ~ "2004-2007",
                         year >= 2022 ~ "2022-2025",
                         TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(era)) %>%
  group_by(era, bin) %>%
  summarise(w = sum(w_sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(era) %>% mutate(share = w / sum(w)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(bin + BIN_PHP / 2, share, fill = era)) +
  geom_col(position = "identity", alpha = 0.55, width = BIN_PHP * 0.92) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2004-2007" = "grey55", "2022-2025" = "#2c7bb6")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Wage-bin distribution relative to the own-region floor: early vs late sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("Nominal P%d bins of (wage - regional total_max), pooled nationally (N8). Bins are era-specific nominal pesos; cross-era comparison is of SHAPE around the floor, not of levels.", BIN_PHP),
       x = sprintf("wage - MW, P%d bins (nominal)", BIN_PHP),
       y = "weighted share", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. Compare shapes, not positions: each era’s bins are its own nominal pesos, so the only valid takeaway is how the distribution organises itself around the floor — the spike at [0, 25) and the depth of the sub-floor shoulder — early versus late in the sample. For level-comparable versions of this picture, the spatially-indexed real bins in the next subsection are the right object.

13.1 Spatially Comparable Real Wage Bins (N13): MW-Anchored, Nationally Summable

The nominal MW-relative bins above cannot be summed across regions or years, and — the sharper problem this document must solve — neither can naive “real 2018 PHP” bins: the CPI indexes each region over time, but a real ₱25 in NCR is not the purchasing power of a real ₱25 in BARMM. Per (N13), the 2018 poverty thresholds supply the missing cross-region price-level index \(\theta_r\); wages and floors are put in NCR-2018-equivalent pesos (\(\tilde w = w^{real}/\theta_r\), \(\tilde M = MW^{real}/\theta_r\)) and binned in ₱25 steps of \(\tilde w - \tilde M\) — distance from the real minimum wage on one common scale. In NCR (\(\theta = 1\)) this is exactly the PoC construction.

# (N13): bin b (left-closed, P25) holds i iff
#           b <= (real_pay_i - real_mw_i) / theta_r < b + 25,
# real_pay = w/defl, real_mw = MW^{tot,max}/defl (N3), theta_r from the
# 2018 poverty thresholds. Unit: NCR-2018-equivalent pesos.
bin_real_obs <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(real_pay = basic_pay_php / defl,
         real_mw  = mw_tot_max / defl,
         rel_s    = (real_pay - real_mw) / theta,
         in_range = rel_s >= BIN_REAL_LO & rel_s < BIN_REAL_HI + BIN_PHP,
         bin      = if_else(in_range, floor(rel_s / BIN_PHP) * BIN_PHP, NA_real_))

cat(sprintf("Share of Sample C outside the [%d, %d) NCR-2018-equivalent range: %.2f%% (weighted)\n",
            BIN_REAL_LO, BIN_REAL_HI + BIN_PHP,
            100 * wshare(!bin_real_obs$in_range, bin_real_obs$weight)))
## Share of Sample C outside the [-300, 625) NCR-2018-equivalent range: 5.72% (weighted)
bin_real_breaks <- seq(BIN_REAL_LO, BIN_REAL_HI, by = BIN_PHP)

bin_panel_real <- bin_real_obs %>%
  filter(in_range) %>%
  group_by(region_wb, year, quarter, ref_date, bin) %>%
  summarise(n_unwt = n(), w_sum = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(region_wb, ref_date) %>%
  mutate(share_wt = w_sum / sum(w_sum)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  complete(nesting(region_wb, year, quarter, ref_date),
           bin = bin_real_breaks,
           fill = list(n_unwt = 0L, w_sum = 0, share_wt = 0)) %>%
  left_join(theta_tbl, by = "region_wb")

write_rds(bin_panel_real, "Output/wage_bin_panel_real_spatial.rds")
write_csv(bin_panel_real, "Output/wage_bin_panel_real_spatial.csv")
cat("Saved spatially-indexed real bin panel:", comma(nrow(bin_panel_real)), "rows\n")
## Saved spatially-indexed real bin panel: 54,057 rows
# National summation (N13): weighted mass per bin summed over ALL regions
# and quarters within each era -- legitimate because every term is in
# NCR-2018-equivalent pesos measured from its own regional real floor.
bin_panel_real %>%
  mutate(era = case_when(year <= 2007 ~ "2004-2007",
                         year >= 2022 ~ "2022-2025",
                         TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(era)) %>%
  group_by(era, bin) %>%
  summarise(w = sum(w_sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(era) %>% mutate(share = w / sum(w)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(bin + BIN_PHP / 2, share, fill = era)) +
  geom_col(position = "identity", alpha = 0.55, width = BIN_PHP * 0.92) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2004-2007" = "grey55", "2022-2025" = "#2c7bb6")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "National real-wage distribution around the real minimum wage (N13)",
       subtitle = wrap_text("P25 bins of (real wage - real MW) / theta, NCR-2018-equivalent pesos. Both eras and all regions live on one purchasing-power scale, so the histograms are directly comparable. Red line = the real floor."),
       x = "wage - minimum wage, NCR-2018-equivalent PHP (P25 bins)",
       y = "weighted share", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. With both eras on one purchasing-power scale, two facts coexist: the at-floor spike persists across two decades, and the sub-floor share of in-range mass moved from 57% (2004–07) to 36% (2022–25). This chart describes where the covered workforce sits relative to its floors; it cannot attribute the change to policy, growth, or composition.

# "Any band is a sum of bins": the +/-P25 spatially-indexed band around the
# real MW is exactly bins -25 and 0; below-band = all b < -25. National
# time series computed purely from the saved panel. (The continuous
# analogue at_real25s in bind_nat differs only by bin discretisation.)
bin_panel_real %>%
  group_by(ref_date, band = case_when(
    bin < -BIN_PHP ~ "More than P25 below the real MW",
    bin %in% c(-BIN_PHP, 0) ~ "Within +/-P25 of the real MW",
    TRUE ~ "More than P25 above the real MW")) %>%
  summarise(w = sum(w_sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(ref_date) %>% mutate(share = w / sum(w)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(band = factor(band, levels = c("More than P25 above the real MW",
                                        "Within +/-P25 of the real MW",
                                        "More than P25 below the real MW"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, share, fill = band)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#a6d96a", "#fdae61", "#d7191c")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "National shares relative to the real minimum wage, +/-P25 spatially-indexed band",
       subtitle = "Computed by summing P25 bins of the saved N13 panel; the band has local width 25 x theta_r in each region's own real pesos.",
       x = NULL, y = "share of covered wage employment", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The stacked view turns the saved panel into a running answer to “how is the covered workforce distributed around the real floor?” — currently 27% within the spatially-indexed ±₱25 band. Because every band is literally a sum of saved bins, any alternative band a policy discussion needs can be recomputed from the artifact without touching microdata.

bin_panel_real %>%
  group_by(region_wb, bin) %>%
  summarise(w = sum(w_sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% mutate(share = w / sum(w)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(bin + BIN_PHP / 2, share)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7bb6", width = BIN_PHP * 0.92) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Real-wage distributions around the real minimum wage, by lineage (pooled)",
       subtitle = "Same NCR-2018-equivalent x-axis in every panel; cross-panel comparison of both shape and position is valid.",
       x = "wage - minimum wage, NCR-2018-equivalent PHP (P25 bins)",
       y = "weighted share")

Reading. This is the one histogram grid where cross-panel position comparisons are legitimate: every axis is NCR-2018-equivalent pesos from the region’s own real floor. Panels with heavier left-of-zero mass are regions where the floor overshoots more of its covered distribution; panels with mass concentrated just right of zero are regions where the floor effectively is the going wage. That cross-region variation in bite is exactly what the event study exploits.

14 The Wage-Increase Event Study (Cengiz-Style)

This section carries the NCR PoC’s event-time wage-bin analysis to its national form, per (N14), with three upgrades the PoC’s feasibility section anticipated: per-capita bin employment instead of shares (shares can only show redistribution; employment impact requires counts against a population denominator), spatially comparable bins (N13, so events in different regions average meaningfully), and — the step NCR alone could never take — timing-based control regions: lineages with no wage order of their own within ±4 quarters of the event, binned against the treated event’s real floor. The honest framing stands: controls are selected on wage-order timing, not random assignment, and no never-treated region exists; this is the closest feasible approximation to Cengiz et al. (2019), not a replication of their identification.

14.1 How the Event–Bin Panel Is Built (and Why It Has To Be Built This Way)

The LFS is a repeated cross-section: different people every quarter, no worker identifiers, no way to follow anyone. That rules out every person-level design (“did worker \(i\) keep their job?”). The Cengiz et al. insight is that the panel unit does not have to be the worker: make it the wage bin. A ₱25 slice of the wage distribution in a given region is followable over time — its employment mass is estimable from every cross-section — and the question “where did the sub-floor jobs go?” becomes an accounting identity over bins. Concretely, the pipeline is:

  1. Person-quarter observations (Sample C: private-establishment, non-agriculture wage workers with positive daily basic pay) carry a wage, a weight, a lineage, and a quarter. Nothing else about the worker is needed.
  2. Common real scale (N13). Each wage is deflated by its own region’s CPI to 2018 pesos, then divided by \(\theta_r\) (2018 poverty-threshold ratio to NCR). Without this step, a “₱25 bin” is a different object in every region and stacking events across regions would add apples to carabaos.
  3. Events (N2 → N14). A wage order enters the analysis on the first LFS round whose reference date is on/after its effectivity (the as-of join), provided the nominal increase is ≥ 3%. The new floor is frozen in the same common unit: \(\tilde M_e = MW^{new} / (\text{defl}_{r,m(t_0)}\,\theta_r)\). Multi-tranche orders appear as separate candidate events per tranche (small tranches usually fail the ≥ 3% screen).
  4. Windows in event time. Each event contributes quarters \(\tau = -4 \dots +7\); post-side quarters at/after the lineage’s next order are censored (they belong to the next event’s story).
  5. Binning. Every person-quarter in a window is assigned to the ₱25 bin of \(\tilde w_i - \tilde M_e\) — distance from that event’s frozen real floor, including in pre-period quarters (where the floor is not yet in force; bins are a fixed ruler, not the prevailing law).
  6. Collapse to the panel. Summing weights within (event, unit, τ, bin) and dividing by the unit’s working-age population WAP\(_{r,t}\) gives per-capita bin employment \(E_{e,\tau,b}\) — the panel outcome. Zero-mass bins are materialised explicitly (complete()), because “no one is paid here anymore” is exactly the signal of interest.
  7. Demeaning. Subtracting each (event, unit, bin)’s own pre-window mean gives \(\Delta E\): how far this bin’s employment sits from its own pre-order level.
  8. Stacking. \(\Delta E\) profiles are averaged across events with equal weights — the same LFS quarter can legitimately serve several overlapping event windows (and treated/control roles for different events); stacking is precisely this reuse, aligned on event time.

Why per-capita counts and not shares. The PoC used within-quarter employment shares per bin; shares always sum to one, so they can only ever show redistribution across bins. Dividing by working-age population instead lets total covered employment move: if sub-floor jobs vanish without reappearing above the floor, per-capita bin masses record it and the cumulative sum ends below zero. That is the entire difference between “the distribution changed shape” and “employment changed.”

What the DiD adds, exactly. The raw stacked contrast (post-mean minus pre-mean) answers: how did the treated region’s wage distribution evolve across the order? Anything else moving at the same time — inflation mechanically pushing nominal wages across a fixed real ruler, seasonal hiring, macro shocks — is absorbed into the answer. The DiD subtracts the same pre/post contrast computed in control lineages: regions with no wage order of their own within ±4 quarters, whose workers are binned against the treated event’s floor \(\tilde M_e\) (a coherent operation only because step 2 put everyone on one scale). Whatever moves wage distributions everywhere — national inflation surprises, seasonality, common growth — differences out; what survives is the treated-minus-control difference in distributional change around the floor.

Is that causal? Under the textbook parallel-trends assumption — absent the wage order, the treated region’s binned distribution would have evolved like the controls’ — the DiD identifies the causal effect of the order on bin employment. That assumption is not credible enough here to claim causality, for reasons the Threats subsection makes specific: control regions exist mainly because their boards chose to freeze (choices concentrated in crises), treated boards chose to raise, and both choices respond to regional conditions. The defensible reading: the raw estimates are descriptive accounting; the DiD estimates are a materially better-adjusted description that nets out common shocks; neither is a randomized experiment, and the pre-trend profile plus the upper-tail placebo are the evidence for how far short of causal each falls in practice.

# (N14) Events from the assigned-rate grid (N2): quarters where mw_tot_max
# rises, screen inc_pct >= EVENT_MIN_NOM_PCT. Contamination calendar (for
# control selection) uses ALL increases, screened or not: any wage order
# moves a would-be control's own floor.
qtr_idx <- qtr_grid %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% arrange(ref_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(qidx = row_number()) %>% ungroup()

all_increases <- qtr_idx %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% arrange(qidx, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(mw_prev = lag(mw_tot_max)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mw_prev), mw_tot_max > mw_prev) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(region_wb, qidx, mw_prev, mw_tot_max, ref_date)

events <- all_increases %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>% arrange(qidx, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(inc_pct = mw_tot_max / mw_prev - 1,
         next_event_qidx = coalesce(lead(qidx), Inf)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(inc_pct >= EVENT_MIN_NOM_PCT) %>%
  transmute(event_id = paste0(region_wb, "_", format(ref_date, "%Y%m")),
            region_wb, t0_qidx = qidx, t0_date = ref_date,
            mw_new = mw_tot_max, mw_prev, inc_pct, next_event_qidx)

# Real, spatially indexed event floor (N14): M_e = mw_new / (defl * theta)
events <- events %>%
  left_join(cpi_defl %>% select(region_wb, cpi_month, defl),
            by = c("region_wb", "t0_date" = "cpi_month")) %>%
  left_join(theta_tbl, by = "region_wb") %>%
  mutate(M_e = mw_new / (defl * theta)) %>%
  select(-defl, -theta)

n_qtrs <- max(qtr_idx$qidx)
events <- events %>%
  mutate(has_pre  = t0_qidx - EVENT_PRE_Q >= 1,
         has_post = t0_qidx + 3 <= n_qtrs & t0_qidx + 3 < next_event_qidx)

# Clean controls per event: lineages with NO increase (of any size) in
# calendar quarters [t0-4, t0+4].
ctrl_pairs <- events %>%
  select(event_id, region_wb, t0_qidx) %>%
  mutate(win_lo = t0_qidx - 4L, win_hi = t0_qidx + 4L) %>%
  crossing(ctrl_wb = factor(REGION_ORDER, levels = REGION_ORDER)) %>%
  filter(ctrl_wb != region_wb) %>%
  anti_join(all_increases %>% select(ctrl_wb = region_wb, c_qidx = qidx),
            by = join_by(ctrl_wb, between(y$c_qidx, x$win_lo, x$win_hi))) %>%
  select(event_id, ctrl_wb)

events <- events %>%
  left_join(ctrl_pairs %>% count(event_id, name = "n_controls"),
            by = "event_id") %>%
  mutate(n_controls = coalesce(n_controls, 0L),
         did_ok = has_pre & has_post & n_controls >= MIN_CONTROLS)

cat("Candidate increases >=", 100 * EVENT_MIN_NOM_PCT, "%:", nrow(events),
    "\n  with full [-4,-1] pre-window:", sum(events$has_pre),
    "\n  also uncensored through tau=+3 (headline set):",
    sum(events$has_pre & events$has_post),
    "\n  additionally with >=", MIN_CONTROLS, "clean controls (DiD set):",
    sum(events$did_ok), "\n")
## Candidate increases >= 3 %: 232 
##   with full [-4,-1] pre-window: 221 
##   also uncensored through tau=+3 (headline set): 158 
##   additionally with >= 3 clean controls (DiD set): 11
events %>%
  filter(has_pre) %>%
  group_by(region_wb) %>%
  summarise(n_events = n(), median_inc_pct = 100 * median(inc_pct),
            n_headline = sum(has_post), n_did = sum(did_ok),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kt("Events by lineage: clean pre-window; headline subset (uncensored through tau=+3); DiD subset (headline + >= 3 timing-based clean controls)", digits = 1)
Events by lineage: clean pre-window; headline subset (uncensored through tau=+3); DiD subset (headline + >= 3 timing-based clean controls)

# Working-age population denominator (all persons 15-64, employed or not)
wap <- lfs %>%
  filter(age_years >= 15, age_years <= 64, !is.na(weight), weight > 0) %>%
  group_by(region_wb, ref_date) %>%
  summarise(wap = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")

# Spatially indexed real wages once, reused for treated and control roles
obs_s <- sample_C %>%
  mutate(w_tilde = basic_pay_php / (defl * theta)) %>%
  select(region_wb, ref_date, w_tilde, weight)

# Event x tau x unit frame. Treated unit: the event's own lineage over
# tau in [-4, +7] (post censored at its next event). Control units: clean
# lineages over tau in [-4, +3] (their own floors are event-free on
# [t0-4, t0+4] by construction, which covers exactly this window).
evt_units <- bind_rows(
  events %>% filter(has_pre) %>%
    transmute(event_id, unit_wb = region_wb, role = "treat",
              t0_qidx, next_event_qidx, M_e),
  events %>% filter(has_pre) %>%
    inner_join(ctrl_pairs, by = "event_id") %>%
    transmute(event_id, unit_wb = ctrl_wb, role = "ctrl",
              t0_qidx, next_event_qidx = Inf, M_e)
)

evt_tau <- evt_units %>%
  crossing(tau = -EVENT_PRE_Q:EVENT_POST_Q) %>%
  filter(role == "treat" | tau <= 3) %>%
  mutate(target_qidx = t0_qidx + tau) %>%
  filter(target_qidx >= 1, target_qidx <= n_qtrs,
         tau < 0 | target_qidx < next_event_qidx) %>%
  left_join(qtr_idx %>% select(unit_wb = region_wb, qidx,
                               target_date = ref_date),
            by = c("unit_wb", "target_qidx" = "qidx"))

# Per-capita bin masses (N14): E = sum(weight in bin) / WAP(unit, quarter),
# bins of (w_tilde - M_e), P25, [-300, 600).
evt_bins_breaks <- seq(EVENT_BIN_LO, EVENT_BIN_HI, by = BIN_PHP)

evt_E <- obs_s %>%
  inner_join(evt_tau %>% select(event_id, role, unit_wb, target_date, tau, M_e),
             by = c("region_wb" = "unit_wb", "ref_date" = "target_date"),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(rel = w_tilde - M_e,
         bin = if_else(rel >= EVENT_BIN_LO & rel < EVENT_BIN_HI + BIN_PHP,
                       floor(rel / BIN_PHP) * BIN_PHP, NA_real_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bin)) %>%
  group_by(event_id, role, region_wb, tau, ref_date, bin) %>%
  summarise(w_sum = sum(weight), n_unwt = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(nesting(event_id, role, region_wb, tau, ref_date),
           bin = evt_bins_breaks, fill = list(w_sum = 0, n_unwt = 0L)) %>%
  left_join(wap, by = c("region_wb", "ref_date")) %>%
  mutate(E = w_sum / wap)

# Delta E per (event, unit, bin): subtract the unit's own pre-window mean
evt_dE <- evt_E %>%
  group_by(event_id, role, region_wb, bin) %>%
  mutate(E_pre = mean(E[tau < 0])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(dE = E - E_pre)

# DiD per (event, tau, bin): treated minus equal-weighted control mean
evt_did <- evt_dE %>%
  group_by(event_id, tau, bin, role) %>%
  summarise(dE = mean(dE), .groups = "drop") %>%   # ctrl mean; treat = itself
  pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = dE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(treat), !is.na(ctrl)) %>%
  mutate(dE_did = treat - ctrl)
# Headline Cengiz figure (raw stacked): Delta E averaged over tau in [0,3],
# equal weights across headline events, in pp of WAP; with the running
# cumulative sum from the lowest bin (its right-edge value = net change
# over the whole displayed range).
headline_ids <- events %>% filter(has_pre, has_post) %>% pull(event_id)

evt_headline <- evt_dE %>%
  filter(role == "treat", event_id %in% headline_ids, tau >= 0, tau <= 3) %>%
  group_by(event_id, bin) %>%
  summarise(dE_post = mean(dE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(dE = 100 * mean(dE_post), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bin) %>%
  mutate(cum_dE = cumsum(dE))

miss_mass <- sum(evt_headline$dE[evt_headline$bin < 0])
xs_mass   <- sum(evt_headline$dE[evt_headline$bin >= 0 & evt_headline$bin < 100])

ggplot(evt_headline, aes(bin + BIN_PHP / 2)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = dE, fill = bin < 0), width = BIN_PHP * 0.92,
           show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_dE), colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cum_dE), colour = "grey25", size = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#d7191c", `FALSE` = "#2c7bb6")) +
  labs(title = "Average change in bin employment around minimum-wage increases (raw stacked, N14)",
       subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
         "Mean over tau = 0..+3 minus mean over tau = -4..-1, equal-weighted across %d headline events; NCR-2018-equivalent P25 bins. Line = cumulative sum from the lowest bin. Missing mass below the floor: %.3f pp of WAP; excess in [0, +P100): %.3f pp.",
         length(headline_ids), miss_mass, xs_mass)),
       x = "wage - new real floor, NCR-2018-equivalent PHP (P25 bins)",
       y = "change in employment, pp of working-age population")

Reading. The signature is present: sub-floor bins lose mass (red), the first bins at/above gain more (blue), and the cumulative line ends near — here slightly above — zero, the accounting statement that mass relocated rather than vanished. Because this is a raw before/after, secular real-wage growth across the fixed ruler is included in the picture; the small positive drift in far-above-floor placebo bins is the visible symptom. The full numeric reading, with confidence intervals, follows in the Interpreting subsection.

# DiD version: treated Delta E minus timing-based clean-control Delta E,
# events with >= MIN_CONTROLS controls, same averaging and display.
did_ids <- events %>% filter(did_ok) %>% pull(event_id)

evt_did_head <- evt_did %>%
  filter(event_id %in% did_ids, tau >= 0, tau <= 3) %>%
  group_by(event_id, bin) %>%
  summarise(dE_post = mean(dE_did), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(dE = 100 * mean(dE_post), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bin) %>%
  mutate(cum_dE = cumsum(dE))

miss_did <- sum(evt_did_head$dE[evt_did_head$bin < 0])
xs_did   <- sum(evt_did_head$dE[evt_did_head$bin >= 0 & evt_did_head$bin < 100])

ggplot(evt_did_head, aes(bin + BIN_PHP / 2)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = dE, fill = bin < 0), width = BIN_PHP * 0.92,
           show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_dE), colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cum_dE), colour = "grey25", size = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#d7191c", `FALSE` = "#2c7bb6")) +
  labs(title = "Difference-in-differences version: treated minus timing-based clean controls",
       subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
         "%d events with >= %d control lineages (no own wage order within +/-4 quarters), controls binned against the treated event's real floor -- meaningful only under the N13 spatial indexing. Missing mass: %.3f pp; excess in [0, +P100): %.3f pp.",
         length(did_ids), MIN_CONTROLS, miss_did, xs_did)),
       x = "wage - new real floor, NCR-2018-equivalent PHP (P25 bins)",
       y = "DiD change in employment, pp of working-age population")

Reading. Netting out control lineages sharpens the trough-and-spike at the floor and enlarges both masses, but the interpretation below applies with force here: this rests on few events, drawn from freeze-adjacent episodes, and the placebo bins do not sit cleanly at zero — so read the shape as better-adjusted description of reallocation around the floor, not as a causal employment estimate.

# Summary table with the PoC's B* grid, the Cengiz headline %-effect, and
# bootstrap CIs over events.
# Per event: Delta_b = sum_{b<0} dE; Delta_a(B*) = sum_{0<=b<B*} dE;
# net(B*) = Delta_b + Delta_a(B*); placebo = sum_{300<=b<600} dE;
# pre_below = pre-window per-capita mass below the new floor (the "affected
# employment" denominator). Headline %-effect (Cengiz):
#     pct_net = 100 * mean(net_100) / mean(pre_below)
# = percent change in affected (below-new-floor) employment. CIs: percentile
# bootstrap resampling EVENTS (N_BOOT draws); the % effect is bootstrapped
# jointly (ratio of resampled means).
event_level <- function(dE_tbl, val_col) {
  dE_tbl %>%
    group_by(event_id) %>%
    summarise(
      d_below   = 100 * sum(.data[[val_col]][bin < 0]),
      d_a100    = 100 * sum(.data[[val_col]][bin >= 0 & bin < 100]),
      d_a200    = 100 * sum(.data[[val_col]][bin >= 0 & bin < 200]),
      d_a300    = 100 * sum(.data[[val_col]][bin >= 0 & bin < 300]),
      d_placebo = 100 * sum(.data[[val_col]][bin >= PLACEBO_LO]),
      .groups = "drop")
}

# Pre-window affected mass (treated units), per event
pre_mass <- evt_dE %>%
  filter(role == "treat") %>%
  distinct(event_id, bin, E_pre) %>%
  group_by(event_id) %>%
  summarise(pre_below = 100 * sum(E_pre[bin < 0]), .groups = "drop")

ev_raw <- evt_dE %>%
  filter(role == "treat", event_id %in% headline_ids, tau >= 0, tau <= 3) %>%
  group_by(event_id, bin) %>% summarise(v = mean(dE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  event_level("v") %>% left_join(pre_mass, by = "event_id")
ev_did <- evt_did %>%
  filter(event_id %in% did_ids, tau >= 0, tau <= 3) %>%
  group_by(event_id, bin) %>% summarise(v = mean(dE_did), .groups = "drop") %>%
  event_level("v") %>% left_join(pre_mass, by = "event_id")

boot_ci <- function(x) {
  bs <- replicate(N_BOOT, mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE)))
  sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", quantile(bs, 0.025), quantile(bs, 0.975))
}
boot_ci_ratio <- function(num, den) {   # CI for 100*mean(num)/mean(den)
  n <- length(num)
  bs <- replicate(N_BOOT, { i <- sample.int(n, replace = TRUE)
                            100 * mean(num[i]) / mean(den[i]) })
  sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", quantile(bs, 0.025), quantile(bs, 0.975))
}
summarise_est <- function(ev, label) {
  net <- ev$d_below + ev$d_a100
  tibble(
    estimator      = label,
    n_events       = nrow(ev),
    pre_below      = mean(ev$pre_below),
    delta_below    = mean(ev$d_below),
    ci_below       = boot_ci(ev$d_below),
    delta_a100     = mean(ev$d_a100),
    ci_a100        = boot_ci(ev$d_a100),
    net_100        = mean(net),
    ci_net100      = boot_ci(net),
    pct_effect     = 100 * mean(net) / mean(ev$pre_below),
    ci_pct         = boot_ci_ratio(net, ev$pre_below),
    delta_a200     = mean(ev$d_a200),
    delta_a300     = mean(ev$d_a300),
    bunch_ratio    = mean(ev$d_a100) / abs(mean(ev$d_below)),
    placebo_300up  = mean(ev$d_placebo),
    ci_placebo     = boot_ci(ev$d_placebo)
  )
}
evt_summary <- bind_rows(summarise_est(ev_raw, "Raw stacked (pre/post)"),
                         summarise_est(ev_did, "DiD vs timing controls"))
evt_summary %>%
  kt("Cengiz-style summary, pp of working-age population unless noted: pre-window affected mass below the new floor; missing mass; excess mass (B* = P100, with P200/P300 in later columns); net low-wage change; pct_effect = 100 x net / pre-affected mass (the Cengiz headline '% change in affected employment'); bunching ratio; upper-tail placebo [P300, P600). Brackets: 95% percentile bootstrap over events.",
     digits = 3)

Brackets: 95% percentile bootstrap over events.

# Time path (raw): Delta-b and Delta-a(100) by event time, averaged over
# events available at each tau (post censoring changes composition).
tau_path <- evt_dE %>%
  filter(role == "treat") %>%
  group_by(event_id, tau) %>%
  summarise(d_below  = 100 * sum(dE[bin < 0]),
            d_excess = 100 * sum(dE[bin >= 0 & bin < 100]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(tau) %>%
  summarise(n_events = n(),
            `Below new floor (missing mass)` = mean(d_below),
            `0 to +P100 above (excess mass)` = mean(d_excess), .groups = "drop")

tau_path %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(tau, n_events)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tau, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2c7bb6", "#d7191c")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -EVENT_PRE_Q:EVENT_POST_Q) +
  labs(title = "Missing and excess mass by event time (raw stacked)",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Averages across events available at each tau; late-tau points average fewer events (censoring at the next wage order). NOTE: demeaning forces each event's pre-window MEAN to zero by construction -- the informative pre-period check is the absence of a TREND (e.g., missing mass already declining before tau = 0 would signal anticipation), not the level."),
       x = "event time tau (quarters relative to the wage order)",
       y = "pp of working-age population", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The dynamics carry the distinctive Philippine finding: both masses jump at τ = 0, then decay toward zero within roughly four to five quarters as inflation and wage growth carry the distribution past the fixed real event-floor — each order’s bite is transient, and the near-annual cadence restarts the cycle. The flat pre-period is consistent with limited anticipation, remembering that only a pre-trend, not the pre-level, is informative here.

14.2 Interpreting the Estimates

The template below is written against the objects just computed, so the sentences update automatically when the document is knit on different data or parameters.

Raw stacked (158 events). In the first year under a new wage order, employment below the new real floor changes by -0.268 pp of working-age population (95% CI [-0.492, -0.066]) against a pre-window affected mass of 9.454 pp, while employment in the first ₱100 at/above the floor changes by 0.432 pp ([0.225, 0.614]). The net low-wage change is 0.164 pp ([-0.016, 0.333]), i.e. 1.7% of pre-order affected employment ([-0.1, 3.5]). A bunching ratio of 1.61 says each percentage point leaving the sub-floor region is matched by 1.61 pp appearing just above it. The upper-tail placebo is 0.039 pp ([0.008, 0.066]): values away from zero mean the raw contrast is also picking up distribution-wide drift (secular real wage growth across the fixed real ruler), so raw magnitudes should not be read as floor-caused.

DiD vs timing controls (11 events). Netting out contemporaneous changes in control lineages, the below-floor change is -1.512 pp ([-3.503, 0.205]) and the excess in [0, ₱100) is 1.262 pp ([0.054, 2.942]); the net effect is -0.250 pp ([-0.856, 0.201]), or -2.2% of affected employment ([-7.0, 1.7]). Read the three CIs together: if the missing- and excess-mass CIs exclude zero while the net CI includes it, the data show clear reallocation across the floor with no detectable employment effect – the Cengiz pattern. A DiD placebo of 0.163 pp ([0.077, 0.268]) materially different from zero is a warning that treated-vs-control differences are not confined to the floor region, so part of the measured masses reflects broader relative-distribution shifts (see Threats, especially control selection), and the DiD should be read as better-adjusted description rather than a causal estimate.

The event-time chart adds the dynamics: in the Philippine setting the excess mass typically decays over \(\tau = 1 \dots 5\) and the missing mass climbs back toward zero — the fixed real event-floor stops binding as inflation and wage growth carry the distribution past it, and the next annual order restarts the cycle. That decay profile is itself a finding: the bite of any single order is transient by construction of the near-annual wage-setting cadence.

14.3 Threats to Validity

Ordered roughly from mechanical to fundamental:

  1. Repeated cross-sections, not workers. Bin masses track positions in the distribution, not persons. “Missing mass” cannot distinguish a worker raised to the floor from one who lost a job while another was hired above it. Composition shifts (formalization, sectoral change, survey redesigns in 2021) move bin masses without any wage-order cause.
  2. Measurement at the floor. Digit heaping (heaping diagnostics), basic-vs-total pay mismatch (COLA), and the min–max rate interval all blur exactly the bins the design cares about. A worker lawfully paid total_min sits “below the floor” when the ruler is total_max.
  3. Bin-range truncation. Mass below −₱300 or above +₱600 (NCR-2018 equivalent) is outside the ledger; the out-of-range share is reported above and tracked per event in the sanity exports.
  4. Anticipation. Orders are petitioned, deliberated, and published before effectivity; employers can adjust at \(\tau = -1\). The as-of anchor also delays mid-quarter orders to the next round, smearing \(\tau = 0\). Both bias the pre-window toward containing treatment.
  5. Endogenous treatment timing. Boards raise floors when regional labor markets can bear it; raw post-minus-pre contrasts therefore load expansion-phase wage growth into “effects.” This is visible in the raw upper-tail placebo.
  6. Endogenous control selection — the deepest problem for the DiD. Control lineages exist mainly because their boards froze, and freezes cluster in crises (2009–10, 2020–21). The DiD therefore compares boards that raised during stress episodes with boards that chose not to — both choices reflecting regional conditions. Parallel trends is a strong assumption exactly where the design needs it; a nonzero DiD placebo is the visible symptom.
  7. Spillovers across “control” borders (SUTVA). Commuting and migration link adjacent regions (NCR–CALABARZON above all); a treated region’s order can move a control region’s wages, contaminating the counterfactual in either direction.
  8. Censoring-induced composition across \(\tau\). Later event-time points average fewer, longer-gap events (freeze-adjacent by construction), so the \(\tau\)-profile mixes dynamics with composition.
  9. Few DiD events. The clean-control screen leaves a small, non-random subset of events (MIN_CONTROLS is a parameter; loosening it trades subset size against control quality). Bootstrap CIs are wide, and they resample events only — survey design (PSU/stratum) uncertainty is not propagated.
  10. The common scale is model-dependent. Everything runs through N13: regional CPIs for time, a fixed 2018 poverty-basket ratio for place. Errors in either deflator translate real wages across bin boundaries mechanically, and \(\theta_r\) is a low-income basket held at 2018 relatives.

14.4 Hidden Validation Exports

A non-rendering validation chunk at the end of the document writes machine-checkable diagnostics to Output/sanity_checks_summary.csv, Output/sanity_event_registry.csv, Output/sanity_bin_reconciliation.csv, and Output/sanity_mw_assignment_sample.csv – internal identities, reconciliations, and per-event audit rows that would clutter this HTML. They are meant to be inspected (or shared) as flat files.

15 Lower-Tail Compression

# Percentile ratios from bind_qtr: p50/p10 (lower tail) and p90/p50 (upper).
bind_qtr %>%
  mutate(`p50 / p10` = p50 / p10, `p90 / p50` = p90 / p50) %>%
  select(region_wb, ref_date, `p50 / p10`, `p90 / p50`) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(region_wb, ref_date)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~region_wb, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("p50 / p10" = "#d7191c", "p90 / p50" = "#2c7bb6")) +
  labs(title = "Wage-distribution percentile ratios by lineage (Sample C)",
       subtitle = "Falling p50/p10 with stable p90/p50 = lower-tail compression, the signature a binding floor (or improving compliance) would produce.",
       x = NULL, y = "ratio", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The lower-tail ratio p50/p10 and the upper-tail ratio p90/p50 answer different questions: a floor that binds should compress the former and leave the latter alone. Panels where p50/p10 hugs a low, flat line are regions where the floor (plus whatever else compresses bottoms) leaves little room between the median and the 10th percentile. Compression is consistent with a binding floor but equally consistent with compressed productivity distributions; this chart cannot separate them.

16 Reconciliation with the NCR Proof of Concept

The NCR PoC’s published numbers used different conventions (its sample included Government/GOCC and Private Household, imposed no industry restriction, and measured the at-band in real ±₱25). This section recomputes NCR under both convention sets on the same underlying data, so any difference between this document’s NCR facet and the PoC is attributable to conventions, not to data or code drift.

# PoC conventions: classes {PE, Gov, PH}, all industries, threshold total_max,
# at-band |real w - real MW| <= 25 (2018 PHP).
# New conventions: Sample C, +/-5% band. Both at Q2 of selected years.
recon_years <- c(2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, 2024)

ncr_poc <- sample_B %>%
  filter(region_wb == "NCR", quarter == 2, year %in% recon_years) %>%
  mutate(real_pay = basic_pay_php / defl, real_mw = mw_tot_max / defl) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(convention = "PoC (B-sample, all industries, real +/-P25)",
            kaitz_med  = first(mw_tot_max) / weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.5),
            F_at_below = wshare(basic_pay_php <= mw_tot_max, weight),
            B_strict   = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_max, weight),
            at_band    = wshare(abs(real_pay - real_mw) <= AT_MW_BAND_PHP_REAL, weight),
            .groups = "drop")

ncr_new <- sample_C %>%
  filter(region_wb == "NCR", quarter == 2, year %in% recon_years) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(convention = "This doc (C-sample, non-agri PE, +/-5%)",
            kaitz_med  = first(mw_tot_max) / weighted_quantile(basic_pay_php, weight, 0.5),
            F_at_below = wshare(basic_pay_php <= mw_tot_max, weight),
            B_strict   = wshare(basic_pay_php <  mw_tot_max, weight),
            at_band    = wshare(abs(basic_pay_php / mw_tot_max - 1) <= AT_MW_BAND_PCT, weight),
            .groups = "drop")

bind_rows(ncr_poc, ncr_new) %>%
  arrange(year, convention) %>%
  kt("NCR at Q2 of selected years under PoC vs. this document's conventions. Differences between the rows of each year-pair are convention effects (sample composition and band definition), computed on identical underlying data.",
     digits = 3)

17 Robustness

17.1 Total vs. basic rates

LFS basic pay may exclude COLA-type allowances that the total_* rates include; comparing it to basic_max is the concept-matched alternative. The gap between the two series bounds the COLA-mismatch effect on measured noncompliance.

bind_nat %>%
  select(ref_date, `below total_max (headline)` = B_max,
         `below basic_max (COLA-matched)` = B_bas_max) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ref_date) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2c7bb6", "#fdae61")) +
  labs(title = "Strict share below the floor: total vs. basic rate thresholds (national)",
       subtitle = wrap_text("Where wage orders grant COLA on top of basic (total > basic), a worker paid the basic rate but reporting basic pay only would appear below total_max though compliant on basic. The gap bounds this mismatch."),
       x = NULL, y = "share of covered wage employment", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The vertical gap between the lines — 0.0 pp in the latest quarter — bounds how much measured “below the floor” could be an accounting artifact of workers reporting basic pay while the ruler includes COLA. Quarters where the gap widens coincide with wage orders that loaded increases into allowances rather than basic rates.

17.2 Band definitions

bind_nat %>%
  select(ref_date, `+/-5% of MW (headline, N6)` = part_at,
         `+/-P25 real, spatially indexed (N13; = PoC in NCR)` = at_real25s) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ref_date) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ref_date, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2c7bb6", "#d7191c")) +
  labs(title = "At-MW share under the two band definitions (national, covered sector)",
       x = NULL, y = "share within band", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

Reading. The two at-band definitions track each other closely, which is the reassurance this chart exists to provide: the headline ±5% convention and the PoC’s spatially-indexed real-₱25 band identify substantially the same group of at-floor workers, so no conclusion in this document hinges on the band choice.

18 Validation Exports (Non-Rendering)

This chunk renders nothing. It recomputes internal identities and writes them, plus per-event and per-cell audit rows, to Output/sanity_*.csv for machine checking outside the HTML.

19 Limitations and Caveats Register

Collected here so no chart has to carry every footnote:

  1. Coverage vs. noncompliance. The LFS cannot observe establishment size (retail/service < 10 workers exemptions), apprentice/learner status, or BMBE registration. “Below MW” therefore includes some workers lawfully paid under special rates; the N5 interval bounds only the multi-rate ambiguity, not these exemptions.
  2. Basic pay vs. total compensation. basic_pay_php excludes overtime, most allowances, 13th-month pay, and tips (correct for testing the statutory floor on basic pay, but not take-home pay). The total-vs-basic robustness chart bounds the COLA side of this.
  3. One rate per lineage. Sub-regional (provincial / area-class) rate differentiation is collapsed to the [total_min, total_max] interval; LFS geography cannot do better (province missing 2019 Q1–2021 Q1, place-of-work-based from 2021 Q2).
  4. NIR seams. NIR observations (2016 Q4, 2025+) are mapped to VI/VII by province; rows with missing province are dropped (counted in the recode validation). The 2023 poverty-threshold vintage excludes Negros from VI/VII while the lineages include it.
  5. Region VIII, 2013 Q4–2015 Q2. Yolanda disrupted enumeration (absent 2014 Q1, reduced samples after); Region VIII series there describe a non-comparable population.
  6. Mid-quarter wage orders. The N2 anchor (first of the reference month) assigns an order effective later in the quarter to the next round; a last-day anchor would shift some assignments by one quarter.
  7. Heaping. The heaping diagnostics’ shares quantify round-number reporting; ±5%-band and at-MW statistics partly reflect it. The off-round split is the cleaner evidence; no fixed heaping level “validates” bunching.
  8. Survey redesigns. The 2021 sample expansion and weight rebasings (visible in the coverage grid and doc-1’s population series) change precision, not concepts; no adjustment is applied.
  9. No standard errors. All statistics are weighted point estimates. Inference requires survey::svydesign(ids = ~psu, strata = ~stratum, nest = TRUE); planned for the causal follow-up, not this descriptive document.
  10. Event study is close-to-Cengiz, not Cengiz. Timing-based controls (no own wage order within ±4 quarters) are selected on wage-order timing, not random assignment; control availability clusters in freeze episodes (2009–10, 2020–21), so the DiD subset is not a random draw of events. Raw pre/post estimates absorb macro shocks entirely. Pre-period profiles and the upper-tail placebo are the internal checks; bootstrap CIs resample events, not survey PSUs.
  11. The spatial index is a poverty-basket index. \(\theta_r\) deflates cross-region price levels with the 2018 poverty-threshold basket, which is a low-income consumption basket — the right basket for wage floors near the poverty line, but not a general spatial PPP. It is also held fixed at 2018 relatives; regional relative price-level drift over 2004–2025 is absorbed by the CPI only to the extent regional CPIs capture it.
  12. CHECK-flagged wage-order rows. Six source rows with effectivity preceding issuance are used as-is (validation table), per the doc-1 convention.
